title.zh: 卷43 嚴棱 毛修之 唐和 劉休賓 房法夀
title.en: Volume 43: Yan Leng, Mao Xiuzhi, Tang He, Liu Xiubin, Fang Fashou
title.raw: 卷43 嚴棱 毛修之 唐和 劉休賓 房法夀 Volume 43: Yan Leng, Mao Xiuzhi, Tang He, Liu Xiubin, Fang Fashou

sentences.zh: 嚴稜 毛脩之 唐和 劉休賓 房法壽

translations.literal: Yan Leng, Mao Xiuzhi, Tang He, Liu Xiubin, Fang Fashou
translations.idiomatic: Yan Leng, Mao Xiuzhi, Tang He, Liu Xiubin, and Fang Fashou

sentences.zh: 嚴稜，馮翊臨晉人。

translations.literal: Yan Leng was a native of Linjin in Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Leng came from Linjin in Fufeng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 遇亂避地河南，劉裕以為廣威將軍、陳留太守，戍倉垣。

translations.literal: When disorder arose he fled south to Henan; Liu Yu appointed him General of Expansive Might and Administrator of Chenliu, garrisoning Cangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Amid the turmoil he took refuge in Henan, where Liu Yu made him General of Expansive Might and Administrator of Chenliu, stationed at Cangyuan.

sentences.zh: 泰常中，山陽公奚斤南討，軍至潁川，稜率文武五百人詣斤降，驛送稜朝太宗於冀州。

translations.literal: In the Taichang era, the Duke of Shanyang Xi Jin marched south in punitive expedition; when his army reached Yingchuan, Leng led five hundred civil and military officials to Xi Jin to surrender, and Leng was sent by post to audience with Emperor Taizong in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taichang reign, Duke Xi Jin of Shanyang led a southern campaign; when his forces reached Yingchuan, Leng brought five hundred officials and officers to submit to Xi Jin, who had him escorted by relay to present himself to Emperor Taizong in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉其誠款，拜平遠將軍，賜爵郃陽侯，假荊州刺史。

translations.literal: His sincerity was commended; he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance, enfeoffed as Marquis of Heyang, and given acting appointment as Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his good faith, appointed him General Who Pacifies the Distance, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Heyang, and granted him acting authority as Inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 隨駕南討，還為上客。

translations.literal: He accompanied the imperial campaign south and on return was made a senior guest.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the emperor on the southern expedition and, upon returning, was received as a distinguished guest at court.

sentences.zh: 及世祖踐阼，以稜歸化之功，除中山太守，有清廉之稱。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu took the throne, in recognition of Leng's merit in submitting to the dynasty he was appointed Administrator of Zhongshan and won repute for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Shizu ascended the throne, Leng was made Administrator of Zhongshan in reward for his surrender and gained a reputation for clean government.

sentences.zh: 年九十，卒於家。

translations.literal: At the age of ninety he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home at the age of ninety.

sentences.zh: 子雅玉，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Yayu inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yayu succeeded to the marquisate.

sentences.zh: 真君中，詔雅玉副長安鎮將元蘭率眾一萬，迎漢川附化之民，入自斜谷，至甘亭。

translations.literal: In the Zhenjun era an edict ordered Yayu to assist the garrison commander of Chang'an, Yuan Lan, in leading ten thousand men to welcome the people of Hanzhong who had submitted, entering by Xiegu and reaching Ganting.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenjun reign he was ordered to assist Yuan Lan, commander of the Chang'an garrison, in leading ten thousand troops to receive Hanzhong people who had come over, marching in through Xiegu as far as Ganting.

sentences.zh: 劉義隆梁州刺史王玄載遣將拒嶮，路不得通，班師。

translations.literal: Liu Yilong's Inspector of Liangzhou Wang Xuanzai sent generals to block the passes; the route could not be opened and the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuanzai, Liu Yilong's Inspector of Liangzhou, sent officers to hold the defiles; the way was blocked and the force turned back.

sentences.zh: 太和二年，太倉令。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taihe he was Grand Steward of the Granary.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taihe he served as Grand Steward of the Granary.

sentences.zh: 五年，出為平南將軍、東兗州刺史，假馮翊公。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he went out as General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Eastern Yanzhou, with acting enfeoffment as Duke of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was posted as General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Eastern Yanzhou, with provisional rank as Duke of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 卒，子曇襲爵。

translations.literal: He died; his son Tan inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his son Tan inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 毛脩之，字敬文，滎陽陽武人也。

translations.literal: Mao Xiuzhi, courtesy name Jingwen, was a native of Yangwu in Yingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xiuzhi, whose courtesy name was Jingwen, came from Yangwu in Yingyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 父瑾，司馬德宗梁秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Jin was Liang and Qin Inspector for Emperor Dezong of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jin had been Inspector of Liang and Qin under Emperor Dezong of Jin.

sentences.zh: 劉裕之擒姚泓，留子義真鎮長安，以脩之為司馬。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu captured Yao Hong he left his son Yizhen to garrison Chang'an and appointed Xiuzhi as Chief Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Yu took Yao Hong captive, he left his son Yizhen to hold Chang'an and made Xiuzhi chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 及赫連屈丐破義真於青泥，脩之被俘，遂沒統萬。

translations.literal: When Helian Quju defeated Yizhen at Qingni, Xiuzhi was taken captive and ended up in Tongwan.
translations.idiomatic: When Helian Quju routed Yizhen at Qingni, Xiuzhi was captured and passed into Helian rule at Tongwan.

sentences.zh: 世祖平赫連昌，獲脩之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu pacified Helian Chang, Xiuzhi was obtained.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu subdued Helian Chang, Xiuzhi came into his hands.

sentences.zh: 神䴥中，以脩之領吳兵討蠕蠕大檀，以功拜吳兵將軍，領步兵校尉。

translations.literal: In the Shenju era Xiuzhi led Wu troops against the Rouran khan Datan; for merit he was appointed General of Wu Troops and Colonel Director of Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenju reign he commanded Wu troops against the Rouran khan Datan and, for his service, was made General of Wu Troops and Colonel Director of Footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 後從世祖征平涼有功，遷散騎常侍、前將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Later he followed Emperor Shizu in the Pingliang campaign with merit and was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of the Vanguard, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He later accompanied Emperor Shizu on the Pingliang campaign, distinguished himself, and rose to Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of the Vanguard, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 脩之能為南人飲食，手自煎調，多所適意。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi could prepare southern-style food and personally cooked and seasoned it, often to great satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi knew how to prepare southern cuisine and cooked and seasoned dishes himself, usually to excellent effect.

sentences.zh: 世祖親待之，進太官尚書，賜爵南郡公，加冠軍將軍，常在太官，主進御膳。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu treated him with personal favor, advanced him to Director of the Imperial Kitchen, enfeoffed him as Duke of Nancheng, added the title General of the Champions, and kept him constantly in the Imperial Kitchen in charge of presenting the imperial meals.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor favored him personally, promoted him to Director of the Imperial Kitchen, enfeoffed him as Duke of Nancheng, gave him the additional title General of the Champions, and kept him in the kitchen service supervising the imperial table.

sentences.zh: 從討和龍，別破三堡，賜奴婢、牛羊。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Helong and separately captured three forts, receiving slaves, cattle, and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: On the Helong campaign he separately reduced three strongholds and was rewarded with slaves, cattle, and sheep.

sentences.zh: 是時，諸軍攻城，宿衞之士多在戰陳，行宮人少。

translations.literal: At that time the various armies were besieging cities and most of the palace guard were in the battle lines, so few remained at the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the armies were investing cities and most of the palace guards were on the front, leaving the mobile court lightly manned.

sentences.zh: 雲中鎮將朱脩之，劉義隆故將也，時從在軍，欲率吳兵謀為大逆，因入和龍，冀浮海南歸。

translations.literal: Zhu Xiuzhi, garrison commander of Yunzhong and a former general of Liu Yilong, was then with the army and wished to lead Wu troops in a great treason, entering Helong in hope of crossing the sea south to return.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xiuzhi, the Yunzhong garrison commander and once a general of Liu Yilong, was with the campaign and plotted to rally Wu troops in a major rebellion, intending to enter Helong and flee by sea back to the south.

sentences.zh: 以告脩之，脩之不聽，乃止。

translations.literal: He told Mao Xiuzhi, but Xiuzhi would not listen and the plot stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He informed Mao Xiuzhi, who refused to go along, and the conspiracy was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 是日無脩之，大變幾作。

translations.literal: Had Xiuzhi not been present that day, a great upheaval would nearly have occurred.
translations.idiomatic: Had Mao Xiuzhi not been there that day, a grave crisis would almost certainly have erupted.

sentences.zh: 朱脩之遂亡奔馮文通。

translations.literal: Zhu Xiuzhi then fled to Feng Wentoong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xiuzhi thereupon fled to Feng Wentoong.

sentences.zh: 又以脩之收三堡功多，遷特進、撫軍大將軍、金紫光祿大夫，位次崔浩之下。

translations.literal: Because Xiuzhi's merit in taking the three forts was great, he was promoted to Special Grand Master, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Grand Master of the Golden Chariot and Purple Canopy, ranking below Cui Hao.
translations.idiomatic: As Xiuzhi's credit for capturing the three forts was great, he was advanced to Special Grand Master, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Grand Master of the Golden Chariot and Purple Canopy, standing in rank just below Cui Hao.

sentences.zh: 浩以其中國舊門，雖學不博洽，而猶涉獵書傳，每推重之，與共論說。

translations.literal: Hao, because he was of an old Chinese house, though his learning was not broad still dipped into books and records and always esteemed him, discussing with him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xiuzhi came from an established Chinese family, Cui Hao valued him even though his scholarship was not wide, and often discussed texts with him.

sentences.zh: 言次，遂及陳壽三國志有古良史之風，其所著述，文義典正，皆揚于王廷之言，微而顯，婉而成章，班史以來無及壽者。

translations.literal: In the course of talk they came to Chen Shou's Records of the Three Kingdoms, which has the manner of the ancient good historians; what he wrote is canonical in meaning and expression, all words proclaimed at the royal court—subtle yet clear, graceful yet formed into chapters; since the History of the Han none has matched Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Their conversation turned to Chen Shou's Records of the Three Kingdoms, which Hao praised as having the spirit of the great ancient historians—elegant, authoritative, and subtle in judgment, unmatched since Ban Gu.

sentences.zh: 脩之曰：「昔在蜀中，聞長老言，壽曾為諸葛亮門下書佐，被撻百下，故其論武侯云『應變將略，非其所長』。」

translations.literal: Xiuzhi said: "Formerly in Shu I heard elders say that Shou had been a clerical aide under Zhuge Liang and was flogged one hundred strokes, so in his account of the Martial Lord he writes that 'in adapting to change and military stratagem he was not at his best.'"
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi said, "When I was in Shu I heard elders say Chen Shou had served Zhuge Liang as a clerk and was beaten a hundred strokes, which is why he wrote of the Martial Lord that 'in adapting to circumstances and grand strategy he was not at his strongest.'"

sentences.zh: 浩乃與論曰：「承祚之評亮，乃有故義過美之譽，案其迹也，不為負之，非挾恨之矣。

translations.literal: Hao then argued with him, saying: "Chengzuo's appraisal of Liang was in fact excessive praise with a hidden meaning; weighed against his deeds it does not wrong him and is not born of private resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Hao replied that Chen Shou's assessment of Zhuge Liang was actually strained praise with a hidden point—that judged by Liang's record it was not unfair and did not arise from personal spite.

sentences.zh: 何以云然？

translations.literal: Why do I say so?
translations.idiomatic: Why do I say this?

sentences.zh: 夫亮之相劉備，當九州鼎沸之會，英雄奮發之時，君臣相得，魚水為喻，而不能與曹氏爭天下，委棄荊州，退入巴蜀，誘奪劉璋，偽連孫氏，守窮踦𨄅之地，僭號邊夷之間。

translations.literal: When Liang served Liu Bei, it was when the Nine Provinces seethed and heroes rose; ruler and minister were as close as fish and water, yet he could not contend with Cao for the realm, abandoned Jingzhou, withdrew into Ba and Shu, enticed and seized Liu Zhang, falsely allied with Sun, and held a crippled corner in the borderlands, usurping title among barbarian margins.
translations.idiomatic: Liang aided Liu Bei at a time when the empire was in turmoil and heroes contended; though ruler and minister were said to be as close as fish and water, he could not vie with Cao Cao for the realm—he abandoned Jingzhou, retreated into Ba and Shu, wrested Liu Zhang's territory by deceit, made a show of alliance with Sun Quan, and held a desperate foothold on the frontier while claiming imperial title among border peoples.

sentences.zh: 此策之下者。

translations.literal: This was the lowest of strategies.
translations.idiomatic: This was among the weakest possible strategies.

sentences.zh: 可與趙他為偶，而以為管蕭之亞匹，不亦過乎？

translations.literal: He may be paired with Zhao Tuo, yet to treat him as the equal of Guan Zhong and Xiao He—is that not excessive?
translations.idiomatic: He might be compared with Zhao Tuo, yet to rank him with Guan Zhong and Xiao He—is that not going too far?

sentences.zh: 謂壽貶亮非為失實。

translations.literal: Thus one may say Shou's lowering of Liang was not untrue to fact.
translations.idiomatic: So Chen Shou's lowering of Liang's stature was not a distortion of the facts.

sentences.zh: 且亮既據蜀，恃山嶮之固，不達時宜，弗量勢力。

translations.literal: Moreover, once Liang held Shu and relied on its mountain defiles, he did not grasp the times and did not measure strength.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, once Liang held Shu behind its mountain barriers, he failed to read the times and misjudged relative power.

sentences.zh: 嚴威切法，控勒蜀人；

translations.literal: With stern law and tight control he constrained the people of Shu;
translations.idiomatic: He imposed harsh laws and tight control on the people of Shu;

sentences.zh: 矜才負能，高自矯舉。

translations.literal: cherishing talent and trusting in his ability, he exalted himself.
translations.idiomatic: trusting in his own talent, he held himself arrogantly aloof.

sentences.zh: 欲以邊夷之眾抗衡上國。

translations.literal: He wished to pit the masses of the borderlands against the central state.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to pit a frontier population against the central realm.

sentences.zh: 出兵隴右，再攻祁山，一攻陳倉，疏遲失會，摧衄而反；

translations.literal: He sent armies into Longyou, twice attacked Qishan, once attacked Chencang, was dilatory and missed his moment, was broken and driven back;
translations.idiomatic: He marched into Longyou, attacked Qishan twice and Chencang once, was slow and lost his openings, and was beaten back in defeat;

sentences.zh: 後入秦川，不復攻城，更求野戰。

translations.literal: Later he entered Qinchuan, no longer besieging cities but instead seeking field battle.
translations.idiomatic: Later he entered Qinchuan, ceased storming walled towns, and sought open battle instead.

sentences.zh: 魏人知其意，閉壘堅守，以不戰屈之。

translations.literal: The Wei knew his intent, shut their forts and held firm, and overcame him without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei commanders understood his aim, closed their walls and stood firm, and wore him down without giving battle.

sentences.zh: 知窮勢盡，憤結攻中，發病而死。

translations.literal: Knowing his strength was spent, he died of illness amid frustrated rage.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw his strength exhausted, frustration consumed him and he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 由是言之，豈合古之善將，見可而進，知難而退者乎？」

translations.literal: From this perspective, how does he accord with the good generals of old who advance when they see opportunity and withdraw when they know difficulty?
translations.idiomatic: On this showing, how does he resemble the great commanders of antiquity who advance when they see advantage and retire when they know the odds are against them?

sentences.zh: 脩之謂浩言為然。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi said Hao's words were correct.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi agreed that Hao was right.

sentences.zh: 太延二年，為外都大官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiyan he was Grand Director of the Outer Kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiyan he became Grand Director of the Outer Kitchen.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰恭公。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Duke Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Duke Gong.

sentences.zh: 脩之在南有四子，唯子法仁入國。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi had four sons in the south; only his son Faren entered the state.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi had four sons in the south, but only his son Faren came into the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 高宗初，為金部尚書，襲爵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozong's reign he was Director of the Gold Department and inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Gaozong's reign he served as Director of the Gold Department and inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 後轉殿中尚書，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Director of the Palace Department and added as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was later moved to Director of the Palace Department with the additional post of Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 法仁言聲壯大，至於軍旅田狩，唱呼處分，振於山谷。

translations.literal: Faren's voice was powerful; in military affairs, hunting, and the like, when he shouted orders they resounded through the valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Faren had a booming voice; on campaign or in the hunt, when he shouted commands they echoed through the hills.

sentences.zh: 和平六年卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Heping he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Heping.

sentences.zh: 贈征東大將軍、南郡王，諡曰威。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made General Who Conquers the East and Prince of Nancheng, with posthumous title Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed General Who Conquers the East and Prince of Nancheng, with the posthumous name Wei.

sentences.zh: 長子猛虎，太安中，為東宮主書，轉中舍人，又遷中散大夫。

translations.literal: His eldest son Menghu in the Tai'an era was master of documents in the Eastern Palace, then transferred to Palace Attendant, then promoted to Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Menghu, during Tai'an, served as master of documents in the Eastern Palace, then as palace attendant, then as Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 初襲爵，為散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He first inherited the title and was Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He first succeeded to the title and held the post of Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 皇興中，蠕蠕犯塞，從顯祖討之，有勇決之稱。

translations.literal: In the Huangxing era, when the Rouran raided the frontier, he followed Emperor Xianzu in the punitive expedition and won the name of courage and resolve.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangxing, when the Rouran invaded the border, he accompanied Emperor Xianzu on the campaign and earned a reputation for bold decision.

sentences.zh: 太和初卒，贈豫州刺史，諡曰康公。

translations.literal: In the beginning of Taihe he died; he was posthumously made Inspector of Yu and given posthumous title Duke Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in Taihe and was posthumously made Inspector of Yu with the posthumous name Duke Gong.

sentences.zh: 子泰寶，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Taibao inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Taibao inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 征虜長史。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk of the General Who Punishes the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief clerk to the General Who Punishes the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 例降為侯。

translations.literal: By precedent the title was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent the rank was reduced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 卒，子乾祐襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Qianyou inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his son Qianyou succeeded.

sentences.zh: 朱脩之者，劉義隆司徒從事中郎。

translations.literal: Zhu Xiuzhi had been Attendant of the Masters of Writing under Liu Yilong's Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xiuzhi had served as Attendant of the Masters of Writing in Liu Yilong's Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 守滑臺，安頡圍之。

translations.literal: He defended Huatai when it was besieged by An Li.
translations.idiomatic: He held Huatai when An Li besieged it.

sentences.zh: 其母在家，乳汁忽出。

translations.literal: His mother at home suddenly produced milk.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, still at home, suddenly began to lactate again.

sentences.zh: 母號慟告家人曰：「我年老，非復有乳汁之時，今忽如此，兒必歿矣。」

translations.literal: The mother wailed and told the household: "I am old and no longer in the time of milk; that this should happen now means my son will surely perish."
translations.idiomatic: She cried out in grief and told the family, "I am too old to nurse again—when this happens unbidden, my son is surely doomed."

sentences.zh: 果以其日為頡所擒。

translations.literal: Indeed on that very day he was captured by Li.
translations.idiomatic: On that very day he was indeed taken by An Li.

sentences.zh: 世祖善其固守，授以內職，以宗室女妻之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu commended his stout defense and gave him an inner-office post, marrying him to a woman of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu praised his stubborn defense, gave him a post in the inner service, and married him to a woman of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 而佞巧輕薄，為人士所賤。

translations.literal: Yet he was fawning, clever, and frivolous, and was despised by gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was obsequious, cunning, and shallow, and men of standing looked down on him.

sentences.zh: 為雲中鎮將。

translations.literal: He was made garrison commander of Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed garrison commander of Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 及入馮文通，文通送之江南。

translations.literal: When he entered Feng Wentoong's territory, Wentoong sent him back to the south.
translations.idiomatic: When he went over to Feng Wentoong, Wentoong sent him on to the southern court.

sentences.zh: 唐和，字稚起，晉昌冥安人也。

translations.literal: Tang He, courtesy name Zhiqi, was a native of Ming'an in Jinchang.
translations.idiomatic: Tang He, whose courtesy name was Zhiqi, came from Ming'an in Jinchang Commandery.

sentences.zh: [1]父繇，以涼土喪亂，民無所歸，推隴西李暠於敦煌，以寧一州。

translations.literal: [1] His father You, because the Liang lands were lost to disorder and the people had nowhere to turn, raised Li Gao at Dunhuang to settle one province.
translations.idiomatic: [1] His father You, when the Liang territories fell into chaos and the people were homeless, installed Li Gao at Dunhuang to restore order in the region.

sentences.zh: 李氏為沮渠蒙遜所滅，和與兄契攜外甥李寶避難伊吾，招集民眾二千餘家，臣於蠕蠕。

translations.literal: When the Li clan was destroyed by Juqu Mengxun, He and his elder brother Qi took their nephew Li Bao in flight to Yiwu, gathered more than two thousand households, and submitted to the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: After the Li house was overthrown by Juqu Mengxun, He and his brother Qi fled with their nephew Li Bao to Yiwu, rallied more than two thousand families, and submitted to the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕以契為伊吾王。

translations.literal: The Rouran made Qi king of Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran made Qi king of Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 經二十年，和與契遣使來降，為蠕蠕所逼，遂擁部落至于高昌。

translations.literal: After twenty years He and Qi sent envoys to surrender; pressed by the Rouran, they then led their tribes to Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: After twenty years He and Qi sent envoys to surrender; harried by the Rouran, they eventually moved their people to Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕遣部帥阿若率騎討和。

translations.literal: The Rouran sent the tribal commander A Ruo with cavalry to attack He.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran dispatched the tribal leader A Ruo with horsemen to strike at He.

sentences.zh: 至白力城，和率騎五百先攻高昌，契與阿若戰歿。

translations.literal: At Baili City He led five hundred horsemen first to attack Gaochang; Qi died fighting A Ruo.
translations.idiomatic: At Baili City He led five hundred riders in a prior assault on Gaochang; Qi fell in battle against A Ruo.

sentences.zh: 和收餘眾，奔前部王國。

translations.literal: He gathered the survivors and fled to the kingdom of the Former Department.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered the survivors and fled to the Former Department kingdom.

sentences.zh: 時沮渠安周屯橫截城，和攻拔之，斬安周兄子樹，又克高寧、白力二城，斬其戍主。

translations.literal: At that time Juqu Anzhou was encamped at Hengjie City; He stormed and took it, beheaded Anzhou's nephew Shu, and also captured the garrison cities of Gaoning and Baili, killing their commandants.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Anzhou was then stationed at Hengjie City; He stormed it, killed Anzhou's nephew Shu, and also took the garrison towns of Gaoning and Baili, executing their defenders.

sentences.zh: 遣使表狀，世祖嘉其誠款，屢賜和。

translations.literal: He sent a memorial of report; Emperor Shizu praised his sincerity and repeatedly rewarded He.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a formal report to court; Emperor Shizu commended his loyalty and rewarded him repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 和後與前部王車伊洛擊破安周，斬首三百。

translations.literal: He later joined the Former Department king Che Yiluo in defeating Anzhou and beheaded three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined Che Yiluo, king of the Former Department, in defeating Anzhou and taking three hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 世祖遣成周公萬度歸討焉耆，詔和與伊洛率所領赴度歸。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu sent the Duke of Chengzhou Wan Duigui to punish Yanqi and ordered He and Yiluo to lead their forces to join Duigui.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Duke Wan Duigui of Chengzhou against Yanqi and ordered He and Yiluo to bring their followers to Duigui.

sentences.zh: 和奉詔。

translations.literal: He received the edict.
translations.idiomatic: He obeyed the edict.

sentences.zh: 會度歸喻下柳驢以東六城，因共擊波居羅城，拔之。

translations.literal: When Duigui reduced the six cities east of Liulü, together they attacked the city of Bojuluo and took it.
translations.idiomatic: When Duigui brought the six cities east of Liulü to terms, they jointly attacked Bojuluo and captured it.

sentences.zh: 後同征龜茲，度歸令和鎮焉耆。

translations.literal: Later on the joint expedition against Kucha, Duigui ordered He to garrison Yanqi.
translations.idiomatic: On the later campaign against Kucha, Duigui left He to hold Yanqi.

sentences.zh: 時柳驢戍主乙真伽率諸胡將據城而叛，和領輕騎一百匹入其城，擒乙真伽，斬之，由是諸胡款附。

translations.literal: At that time the garrison commander of Liulü, Yizhenjia, led the various Hu in rebellion to hold the city; He entered the city with one hundred light horsemen, seized Yizhenjia, and beheaded him, whereupon the various Hu submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liulü garrison commander Yizhenjia rallied the frontier peoples in revolt, He rode into the city with a hundred light cavalry, seized and executed Yizhenjia, and the tribes then submitted.

sentences.zh: 西域克平，和有力也。

translations.literal: When the Western Regions were pacified, He had great part in it.
translations.idiomatic: He played a major role in the pacification of the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 子欽，字孟直。

translations.literal: His son Qin, courtesy name Mengzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qin, whose courtesy name was Mengzhi.

sentences.zh: 中書學生，襲爵。

translations.literal: A student of the Directorate of Documents, he inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Trained in the Directorate of Documents, he inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 太和中，拜鎮南將軍、長安鎮副將，轉陝州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he was appointed General Who Guards the South and deputy commander of the Chang'an garrison, then transferred to Inspector of Shanzhou, retaining his general's title.
translations.idiomatic: During Taihe he was made General Who Guards the South and deputy commander of the Chang'an garrison, then Inspector of Shanzhou while keeping his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 後降爵為侯。

translations.literal: Later his enfeoffment was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Later his noble rank was reduced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 二十年卒。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twentieth year.

sentences.zh: 子景宣，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Jingxuan inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingxuan inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 歷并州城陽王徽後軍府長史，加中堅將軍，遷東郡太守。

translations.literal: He successively served as chief clerk in the rear army office of Prince Hui of Chengyang in Bingzhou, was added as General of Firm Resolve, and was promoted to Administrator of Dongjun.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as chief clerk in the rear army staff of Prince Hui of Chengyang in Bingzhou, was given the additional title General of Firm Resolve, and became Administrator of Dongjun.

sentences.zh: 普泰中卒。

translations.literal: He died in the Putai era.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Putai era.

sentences.zh: 贈撫軍將軍、秦州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Qin.

sentences.zh: 景宣弟季弼，武定中，滄州別駕。

translations.literal: Jingxuan's younger brother Jibi, in the Wuding era, was Vice-Prefect of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan's younger brother Jibi served as Vice-Prefect of Cangzhou during the Wuding reign.

sentences.zh: 契子玄達，性果毅，有父風。

translations.literal: Qi's son Xuanda was resolute by nature and had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's son Xuanda was bold and decisive, with his father's bearing.

sentences.zh: 與叔父和歸闕，俱為上客。

translations.literal: He returned to court with his uncle He and both were made senior guests.
translations.idiomatic: He came to court with his uncle Tang He, and both were received as distinguished guests.

sentences.zh: 拜安西將軍、晉昌公。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Duke of Jinchang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and enfeoffed as Duke of Jinchang.

sentences.zh: 顯祖時，出為華州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xianzu he went out as Inspector of Huazhou, retaining his general's title.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xianzu he was posted as Inspector of Huazhou while keeping his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 杏城民蓋平定聚眾為逆，顯祖遣給事楊鍾葵擊平定，不克而還，詔玄達討平之。

translations.literal: The people of Xingcheng, Gai Pingding, gathered a crowd in rebellion; Emperor Xianzu sent the attendant Yang Zhongkui to attack Pingding, but he could not overcome him and returned, and an edict ordered Xuanda to pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gai Pingding of Xingcheng raised a rebel band, the emperor sent Attendant Yang Zhongkui against him; Zhongkui failed and withdrew, and Xuanda was ordered to finish the campaign.

sentences.zh: 杏城民成赤李又聚黨，自號為王，逼掠郡縣，殘害百姓。

translations.literal: The Xingcheng man Cheng Chil again gathered a party, styled himself king, pressed and plundered commanderies and counties, and harmed the people.
translations.idiomatic: Another Xingcheng leader, Cheng Chil, rallied followers, declared himself king, raided the districts, and terrorized the populace.

sentences.zh: 玄達率騎二百，邀其狹路，擊破之。

translations.literal: Xuanda led two hundred horsemen, intercepted them on a narrow road, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanda took two hundred cavalry, ambushed them in a defile, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 叛民曹平原復聚為亂，玄達追擊悉平之。

translations.literal: The rebel Cao Pingyuan again gathered in disorder; Xuanda pursued and fully pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel Cao Pingyuan rose again, Xuanda pursued and crushed the movement entirely.

sentences.zh: 延興三年，有罪免官。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yanxing he was guilty and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yanxing he was found guilty and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 太和十六年，降爵為侯。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Taihe his title was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Taihe his noble rank was reduced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子崇，字繼祖，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Chong, courtesy name Jizu, inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chong, whose courtesy name was Jizu, succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 盛樂太守。

translations.literal: Administrator of Shengle.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Administrator of Shengle.

sentences.zh: 崇弟興業，定陽、闡熙二郡太守。

translations.literal: Chong's younger brother Xingye was Administrator of the two commanderies of Dingyang and Chanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's younger brother Xingye held the posts of Administrator of Dingyang and Chanxi.

sentences.zh: 劉休賓，字處幹，本平原人。

translations.literal: Liu Xiubin, courtesy name Chugan, was originally a man of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiubin, whose courtesy name was Chugan, was originally from Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 祖昶，從慕容德度河，家于北海之都昌縣。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chang followed Murong De across the river and settled the family in Duchang County of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chang accompanied Murong De across the Yellow River and established the family in Duchang County in Beihai.

sentences.zh: 父奉伯，劉裕時北海太守。

translations.literal: His father Fengbo was Administrator of Beihai under Liu Yu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fengbo had been Administrator of Beihai under Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 休賓少好學，有文才，兄弟六人，乘民、延和等皆有時譽。

translations.literal: Xiubin from youth loved learning and had literary talent; among six brothers, Chenmin, Yanhe, and others all had contemporary repute.
translations.idiomatic: Xiubin loved study from youth and had literary gifts; of six brothers, Chenmin, Yanhe, and the rest all enjoyed contemporary renown.

sentences.zh: 休賓為劉彧虎賁中郎將，稍遷幽州刺史，鎮梁鄒。

translations.literal: Xiubin was Tiger Guard General of the Household for Liu Yu, then gradually promoted to Inspector of Youzhou, garrisoning Liangzou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiubin served Liu Yu as General of the Tiger Guards of the Household, then rose to Inspector of Youzhou, stationed at Liangzou.

sentences.zh: 及慕容白曜軍至升城，遣人說之，令降，休賓不從。

translations.literal: When Murong Baiyao's army reached Shengcheng he sent men to persuade him to surrender; Xiubin would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Baiyao's army reached Shengcheng, he sent envoys urging surrender, but Xiubin refused.

sentences.zh: 劉彧龍驤將軍崔靈延、行勃海郡房靈建等數十家皆入梁鄒，同舉休賓為征虜、兗州。

translations.literal: Liu Yu's General of the Dragon Cavalry Cui Lingyan, Acting Administrator of Bohai Fang Lingjian, and several tens of families all entered Liangzou and together raised Xiubin as General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Lingyan, Liu Yu's General of the Dragon Cavalry, Fang Lingjian, acting Administrator of Bohai, and dozens of other families entered Liangzou and jointly proclaimed Xiubin General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 會劉彧遣使授休賓輔國將軍、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Yu sent envoys appointing Xiubin General Who Supports the State and Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu then sent envoys confirming Xiubin as General Who Supports the State and Inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 休賓妻，崔邪利女也，生一男，字文曄。

translations.literal: Xiubin's wife was the daughter of Cui Xieli; she bore one son, courtesy name Wenye.
translations.idiomatic: Xiubin's wife was a daughter of Cui Xieli; their son's courtesy name was Wenye.

sentences.zh: 崔氏先歸寧在魯郡，邪利之降也，文曄母子遂與俱入國。

translations.literal: The Cui woman had earlier returned home to her parents in Lu Commandery; when Xieli surrendered, Wenye and his mother then entered the state together.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cui had earlier gone home to Lu Commandery; when Xieli submitted, Wenye and his mother came into the Northern Wei together.

sentences.zh: 至是，白曜表請崔與文曄。

translations.literal: At this time Baiyao memorialized requesting the Cui family and Wenye.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao now petitioned to have Lady Cui and Wenye brought forward.

sentences.zh: 既至，白曜以報休賓，又於北海執延和妻子，送至梁鄒，巡視城下。

translations.literal: When they arrived, Baiyao informed Xiubin; he also seized Yanhe's wife in Beihai and sent her to Liangzou to be displayed below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Once they arrived, Baiyao notified Xiubin; he also took Yanhe's wife captive in Beihai and paraded her before the walls of Liangzou.

sentences.zh: 休賓答白曜，許歷城降，當即歸順，密遣兼主簿尹文達向歷城，觀國軍形勢。

translations.literal: Xiubin replied to Baiyao that he would surrender Licheng and at once submit, secretly sending his chief clerk Yin Wenda to Licheng to observe the state army's strength.
translations.idiomatic: Xiubin answered Baiyao that he would surrender Licheng and submit promptly, while secretly dispatching Chief Clerk Yin Wenda to Licheng to spy on the imperial forces.

sentences.zh: 文達詣白曜，詐言聞王臨境，故來祗候。

translations.literal: Wenda went to Baiyao and falsely said that hearing the king had come to the border, he had come to pay respects.
translations.idiomatic: Wenda approached Baiyao and pretended he had come to pay his respects upon hearing the prince had reached the frontier.

sentences.zh: 私謂白曜曰：「劉休賓父子兄弟，累郡連州，今若識運知機，束手歸化，不審明王加何賞敍？」

translations.literal: Privately he said to Baiyao: "Liu Xiubin, father, sons, and brothers, have held successive commanderies and prefectures; if they now recognize the times and know opportunity and submit with bound hands, I do not know what rewards the enlightened king would grant."
translations.idiomatic: In private he asked Baiyao, "The Liu Xiubin clan has held one post after another—if they now read the times and surrender willingly, what honors would Your Highness grant them?"

sentences.zh: 白曜曰：「休賓仕南，爵寵如此，今若不勞兵甲望風自降者，非直處卿富貴，兼還其婦兒。

translations.literal: Baiyao said: "Xiubin served the south with such rank and favor; if now without troubling arms he surrenders of his own accord, not only will you enjoy wealth and honor, but your wife and child will also be returned.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao replied, "Xiubin enjoyed high rank in the south; if he yields without a fight, not only will you prosper, but your wife and son will be restored to you as well.

sentences.zh: 休賓縱令不畏攻圍，豈不憐其妻子也！

translations.literal: Even if Xiubin is not afraid of siege, does he not pity his wife and children!
translations.idiomatic: Even if Xiubin fears no assault, surely he pities his wife and child!

sentences.zh: 今在升城，[2]卿自往見。」

translations.literal: They are now in Shengcheng; [2] you yourself go see them."
translations.idiomatic: They are in Shengcheng now; [2] go see them yourself."

sentences.zh: 文達乃至升城，見休賓妻子。

translations.literal: Wenda then went to Shengcheng and saw Xiubin's wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Wenda went on to Shengcheng and met Xiubin's family.

sentences.zh: 文曄攀援文達，哭泣號咷，以爪髮為信。

translations.literal: Wenye clung to Wenda, weeping and wailing, and gave nail parings and hair as tokens.
translations.idiomatic: Wenye clung to Wenda, crying loudly, and sent fingernail parings and locks of hair as proof.

sentences.zh: 文達回還，復經白曜，誓約而去。

translations.literal: Wenda returned, again passed by Baiyao, made a sworn pact, and left.
translations.idiomatic: On his way back Wenda stopped again at Baiyao's camp, exchanged oaths, and departed.

sentences.zh: 白曜曰：「卿是休賓耳目腹心，親見其妻子，又知我眾旅少多，善共量議，自求多褔。」

translations.literal: Baiyao said: "You are Xiubin's eyes, ears, heart, and belly; you have seen his wife and children in person and also know how many or few our troops are—deliberate well with him and seek your own greater blessing."
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao told him, "You are Xiubin's trusted agent—you have seen his family and know our strength; weigh matters carefully with him and secure the best outcome you can."

sentences.zh: 文達還見休賓，出其妻兒爪髮，兼宣白曜所言及國軍形勢，謂休賓曰：「升城已敗，歷城非朝則夕，公可早圖之。」

translations.literal: Wenda returned and saw Xiubin, produced his wife's and child's nail parings and hair, and also conveyed Baiyao's words and the state army's situation, saying to Xiubin: "Shengcheng has fallen; Licheng cannot last more than a day or two—you should plan early."
translations.idiomatic: Back in Liangzou, Wenda showed the tokens and reported Baiyao's message and the imperial army's strength, urging Xiubin, "Shengcheng is lost and Licheng will fall within days—you must act soon."

sentences.zh: 休賓撫爪髮泣涕曰：「妻子幽隔，誰不愍乎？

translations.literal: Xiubin stroked the nail parings and hair and wept, saying: "Wife and children separated—who would not pity them?
translations.idiomatic: Xiubin caressed the tokens and wept, "My family is held hostage—who would not grieve for them?

sentences.zh: 吾荷南朝厚恩，受寄邊任，今顧妻子而降，於臣節足乎！」

translations.literal: I bear the southern court's thick grace and was entrusted with a frontier post; to turn now for wife and children and surrender—does that satisfy the minister's integrity!
translations.idiomatic: Yet the southern court favored me greatly and entrusted me with the frontier—if I surrender for my family's sake, where is a minister's honor?

sentences.zh: 然而密與其兄子聞慰議為降計。

translations.literal: Yet secretly with his nephew Wen Wei he discussed a plan to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Still, he secretly discussed surrender with his nephew Wen Wei.

sentences.zh: 聞慰曰：「此故當文達誑詐耳。

translations.literal: Wen Wei said: "This is surely Wenda's deceit.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Wei said, "This must be Wenda's trickery.

sentences.zh: 年常抄掠，豈有多軍也？

translations.literal: Year after year they raid—how could they have so many troops?
translations.idiomatic: They raid us every year—how could they field a huge army?

sentences.zh: 但可撫強兵，勤肅衞，方城狹嶮，何為便生憂怯，示人以弱也。」

translations.literal: Only train strong soldiers, keep strict guard, the terrain is narrow and perilous—why at once grow anxious and timid and show weakness to others?"
translations.idiomatic: Train the troops, tighten the defenses—the terrain is rugged; why grow frightened at once and show the enemy we are weak?"

sentences.zh: 休賓又謂文達曰：「卿勿憚危苦，更為吾作一返，善觀形勢。」

translations.literal: Xiubin also told Wenda: "Do not fear hardship; make another trip for me and observe the situation well."
translations.idiomatic: Xiubin also told Wenda, "Do not shrink from the danger—make another journey and watch the situation closely."

sentences.zh: 於是遣文達偷道而出，令與白曜為期，剋日許送降款。

translations.literal: He then sent Wenda out by a secret path and had him fix a date with Baiyao for delivering the surrender document.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wenda out by a hidden route to set a date with Baiyao for handing over the surrender pledge.

sentences.zh: 文達既至，白曜喜曰：「非直休賓父子荷榮，城內賢豪，亦隨人補授。

translations.literal: When Wenda arrived, Baiyao rejoiced and said: "Not only will Xiubin father and son receive honor, but worthy men in the city will also receive appointments according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenda arrived, Baiyao rejoiced, "Not only will the Xiubin family be honored, but the city's leading men will receive posts as well.

sentences.zh: 卿便即為梁鄒城主。」

translations.literal: You at once shall be lord of Liangzou city."
translations.idiomatic: You shall be made lord of Liangzou at once."

sentences.zh: 以酒灌地，啟告山河曰：「若負休賓，使我三軍覆沒！」

translations.literal: He poured wine on the ground and declared to the mountains and rivers: "If I betray Xiubin, may my three armies be destroyed!"
translations.idiomatic: He poured wine on the ground and swore to heaven and earth, "If I break faith with Xiubin, may my whole army perish!"

sentences.zh: 初，白曜之表取休賓妻子也，顯祖以道固既叛，詔授休賓持節、平南將軍、冀州刺史、平原公。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Baiyao had memorialized to take Xiubin's wife and children, because Dao Gu had already rebelled, Emperor Xianzu issued an edict appointing Xiubin Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the South, Inspector of Jizhou, and Duke of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Baiyao had earlier asked for Xiubin's family, Dao Gu had already rebelled, and the court had appointed Xiubin Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the South, Inspector of Jizhou, and Duke of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 至是，付文達詔策。

translations.literal: Now he handed Wenda the edict and patent.
translations.idiomatic: He now gave Wenda the edict and commission.

sentences.zh: 文達還，謂休賓曰：「白曜信誓如此，公可早為決計，恐攻逼之後，降悔無由。」

translations.literal: Wenda returned and told Xiubin: "Baiyao's sworn faith is such; you should decide soon, lest after assault there be no chance for repentant surrender."
translations.idiomatic: Wenda returned and urged Xiubin, "Baiyao's oath is firm—decide quickly, or after a siege you may have no chance to surrender."

sentences.zh: 休賓於是告兄子聞慰曰：「事勢可知，汝早作降書。」

translations.literal: Xiubin then told his nephew Wen Wei: "The situation is clear—write the surrender document at once."
translations.idiomatic: Xiubin then told Wen Wei, "The matter is obvious—draft the surrender letter now."

sentences.zh: 聞慰沉疑，固執不作，[3]遂差本契。

translations.literal: Wen Wei hesitated and stubbornly would not write; [3] thus the original pact was missed.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Wei wavered and refused to write; [3] the agreed plan was therefore broken.

sentences.zh: 白曜尋遣著作佐郎許赤虎夜至梁鄒南門下，告城上人曰：「汝語劉休賓，何由遣文達頻造僕射，許送降文，歸誠大化，何得無信，違期不來！」

translations.literal: Baiyao soon sent Editorial Assistant Xu Chihu at night to the south gate of Liangzou and told those on the wall: "Tell Liu Xiubin: why did he send Wenda repeatedly to the Minister's camp promising a surrender document and returning to the great transformation, yet be faithless and not come on the appointed day!"
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao soon sent Editorial Assistant Xu Chihu by night to Liangzou's south gate, calling up, "Tell Liu Xiubin: why did he send Wenda again and again to my camp promising surrender, yet break faith and fail to appear on the appointed day!"

sentences.zh: 於是門人唱告，城內悉知，遂相維持，欲降不得，皆云：「劉休賓父子，欲以我城內人易榮位也。」

translations.literal: Then gate guards shouted the news and everyone in the city knew; they mutually restrained one another so they could not surrender, all saying: "Liu Xiubin father and son wish to trade the people of our city for their own glory."
translations.idiomatic: The guards shouted the message and the whole city learned of it; the garrison restrained one another from surrendering, saying, "The Xiubins mean to buy their honors with our lives."

sentences.zh: 尋被攻逼，經冬至春。

translations.literal: Soon they were pressed by attack from winter through spring.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the siege pressed from winter into spring.

sentences.zh: 歷城降，白曜遣道固子景業與文曄至城下。

translations.literal: When Licheng surrendered, Baiyao sent Dao Gu's son Jingye and Wenye below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: When Licheng fell, Baiyao sent Dao Gu's son Jingye and Wenye to the foot of the walls.

sentences.zh: 休賓知道固降，乃出請命。

translations.literal: Xiubin learned that Dao Gu had surrendered and then came out to beg for his fate.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Dao Gu had submitted, Xiubin came out to beg mercy.

sentences.zh: 白曜送休賓及宿有名望者十餘人，俱入代都為客。

translations.literal: Baiyao sent Xiubin and more than ten men of longstanding repute, all into the capital as guests.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao sent Xiubin and a dozen other men of note to the capital as honored guests.

sentences.zh: 及立平齊郡，乃以梁鄒民為懷寧縣，休賓為縣令。

translations.literal: When Pingqi Commandery was established, the people of Liangzou were made Huaining County and Xiubin was made county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: When Pingqi Commandery was organized, Liangzou's people became Huaining County and Xiubin was made magistrate.

sentences.zh: 延興二年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Yanxing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Yanxing.

sentences.zh: 文曄，有志尚，綜覽羣書，輕財重義。

translations.literal: Wenye had high aims, surveyed many books, and valued righteousness over wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Wenye was ambitious, widely read, and prized integrity above money.

sentences.zh: 太和中，坐從兄聞慰南叛，與二弟文顥、季友被徙北邊，高祖特聽還代。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, because his cousin Wen Wei rebelled southward, he and his two younger brothers Wenhao and Jiyou were exiled to the northern frontier; Emperor Gaozu specially allowed them to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: During Taihe, when his cousin Wen Wei defected south, Wenye and his brothers Wenhao and Jiyou were banished north, until Emperor Gaozu specially permitted their return.

sentences.zh: 高祖曾幸方山，文曄大言於路側曰：「求見聖明，申宣久屈。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu once visited Fangshan, Wenye cried out loudly by the roadside: "I seek audience with the sage ruler to declare long-standing grievance."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Fangshan, Wenye shouted from the roadside, "I beg audience with the sage ruler to lay out long-suppressed wrongs."

sentences.zh: 高祖遣尚書李沖宣詔問曰：「卿欲何言，聽卿面自申盡。」

translations.literal: The emperor sent Minister of Documents Li Chong with an edict asking: "What do you wish to say? You may speak fully to my face."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Li Chong of the Secretariat with an edict: "Speak your mind—you may plead your case in person."

sentences.zh: 於是引見。

translations.literal: He was then led in for audience.
translations.idiomatic: He was then brought in for audience.

sentences.zh: 文曄對曰：「臣之陋族，出自平原，往因燕亂，流離河表，居齊以來，八、九十載。

translations.literal: Wenye replied: "My humble clan comes from Pingyuan; formerly because of Yan disorder we were displaced south of the river and have lived in Qi for eighty or ninety years.
translations.idiomatic: Wenye answered, "My humble clan came from Pingyuan; during the Yan turmoil we fled south of the river and have lived in Qi for eighty or ninety years.

sentences.zh: 真君十一年，世祖太武皇帝巡江之日，時年二歲，隨外祖魯郡太守崔邪利於鄒山歸國。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhenjun, on the day Emperor Taizu Shizu toured the Yangzi, I was two years old and followed my maternal grandfather Cui Xieli, Administrator of Lu Commandery, in submitting at Zou Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Zhenjun, when Emperor Taizu toured the Yangzi, I was two and followed my grandfather Cui Xieli, Administrator of Lu, in surrendering at Zou Mountain.

sentences.zh: 邪利蒙賜四品，除廣寧太守。

translations.literal: Xieli received enfeoffment at the fourth rank and was appointed Administrator of Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: Xieli received a fourth-rank enfeoffment and was made Administrator of Guangning.

sentences.zh: 以臣年小，不及齒錄。

translations.literal: Because I was young I was not entered in the registers.
translations.idiomatic: Because I was still a child I was not recorded in the rolls.

sentences.zh: 至天安之初，皇威遠被，臣亡父休賓，劉氏持節、兗州刺史，戍梁鄒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tian'an, when imperial might reached far, my late father Xiubin, Liu's Bearer of the Staff and Inspector of Yanzhou, garrisoned Liangzou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tian'an, when imperial power extended everywhere, my late father Xiubin, the Liu court's Bearer of the Staff and Inspector of Yanzhou, held Liangzou.

sentences.zh: 時慕容白曜以臣父居全齊之要，水陸道衝，青冀二城，往來要路，三城岳跱，並拒王師。

translations.literal: At that time Murong Baiyao, because my father held the key of all Qi, the land-and-water thoroughfare, and the two cities of Qing and Ji were the coming-and-going route—with three cities towering like peaks, all resisting the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Baiyao saw that my father held the strategic heart of Qi, where land and water routes met and the Qing and Ji corridor lay open—three great cities stood like peaks, all defying the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 白曜知臣母子先在代京，表請臣母子慰勞。

translations.literal: Baiyao knew my mother and I were already in the capital and memorialized to have us sent to comfort and encourage.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing my mother and I were already in the capital, Baiyao petitioned to have us sent to negotiate.

sentences.zh: 臣即被先帝詔，遣乘傳詣軍，又賜亡父官爵。

translations.literal: I then received the former emperor's edict and was sent by relay to the army; my late father's office and title were also granted.
translations.idiomatic: I received the late emperor's edict and was dispatched by post to the front; my father's offices were also confirmed.

sentences.zh: 白曜遣右司馬盧河內等送臣母子至鄒。

translations.literal: Baiyao sent Right Chief Commandant Lu Henei and others to escort my mother and me to Zou.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao sent Right Chief Commandant Lu Henei and others to escort us to Zou.

sentences.zh: 臣既見亡父，備申皇澤。

translations.literal: When I saw my late father I fully reported the imperial grace.
translations.idiomatic: When I met my father I conveyed the emperor's favor in full.

sentences.zh: 云：『吾蒙本朝寵遇，捍禦藩屏，尊卑百口，並在二城。

translations.literal: He said: "I have received this court's generous treatment and defend the frontier screen; more than a hundred of high and low rank are in both cities.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "This court has favored me and entrusted me with the frontier; more than a hundred of our kin are in the two cities."

sentences.zh: 吾若先降，百口必被誅滅，既不固誠於本朝，又令尊卑塗炭，豈堪為人臣以奉大魏乎？

translations.literal: If I surrender first, the hundred mouths will surely be put to death; I would neither hold loyal to this court nor spare my kin ruin—how could I serve as a minister and offer allegiance to great Wei?
translations.idiomatic: If I yield first, they will all be killed; I would betray my sovereign and doom my family—how could I then serve Great Wei in good faith?

sentences.zh: 汝且申吾意白僕射，降意已判，平歷城，即率士眾送款軍前。』

translations.literal: You should convey my meaning to the Minister: my intent to surrender is settled; once Licheng is pacified I will lead the masses and deliver the pledge before the army."
translations.idiomatic: Tell the Minister my decision is made: once Licheng falls I will lead the people out to submit."

sentences.zh: 既克歷城，白曜遣赤虎送臣并崔道固子景業等向梁鄒。

translations.literal: Once Licheng was taken, Baiyao sent Chihu to escort me together with Cui Dao Gu's son Jingye and others toward Liangzou.
translations.idiomatic: After Licheng fell, Baiyao sent Chihu with me, Cui Dao Gu's son Jingye, and others to Liangzou.

sentences.zh: 亡父既見赤虎之信，仰感聖朝遠遣妻子，又知天命有歸，擁眾一萬，以城降款。

translations.literal: My late father, having seen Chihu's message, was moved that the sage court had sent his wife and children from afar and also knew that Heaven's mandate had shifted; he led ten thousand men and surrendered the city with a pledge.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Chihu's message, my father was moved that the court had sent his family from afar and recognized the turn of fate; he led ten thousand men in surrender.

sentences.zh: 乘驛赴臺，蒙為客例。

translations.literal: He rode post to the capital and received treatment as a guest.
translations.idiomatic: He rode post to the capital and was received as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 臣私釁深重，亡父以延興二年孤背明世，血誠微心，未獲申展。

translations.literal: My private guilt is heavy: my late father in the second year of Yanxing died alone, abandoning the enlightened age; sincere heart and blood loyalty were never expressed.
translations.idiomatic: My own guilt runs deep: my father died in the second year of Yanxing before his loyalty could be rewarded.

sentences.zh: 如臣等比，並蒙榮爵，為在事孤抑，以人廢勳。」

translations.literal: Men like me have all received noble titles, yet we suffer isolation and suppression in service, our merit discarded for personal reasons.
translations.idiomatic: Men like me were ennobled, yet we remain sidelined and our merit set aside for personal reasons."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「卿訴父賞而卿父無勳。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You plead reward for your father, yet your father had no merit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You ask honors for your father, but your father earned no merit.

sentences.zh: 歷城齊之西關，歸命請順。

translations.literal: Licheng was Qi's western pass and came to allegiance requesting submission.
translations.idiomatic: Licheng was Qi's western gate and submitted willingly.

sentences.zh: 梁鄒小戍，豈能獲全？

translations.literal: Liangzou was a small garrison—how could it have been preserved whole?
translations.idiomatic: Liangzou was a minor post—how could it have held out?

sentences.zh: 何足以為功也。」

translations.literal: How is that enough to count as merit?"
translations.idiomatic: How does that amount to merit?"

sentences.zh: 文曄對曰：「誠如聖旨，愚臣所見，猶有未申。

translations.literal: Wenye replied: "Truly as Your Majesty says; yet in this foolish subject's view there is still more to declare.
translations.idiomatic: Wenye answered, "Your Majesty is right, yet this humble servant still has more to say.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: How so?

sentences.zh: 昔樂毅破齊七十餘城，唯有即墨獨在，此豈非根亡而條立？

translations.literal: Formerly Yue Yi took more than seventy cities of Qi and only Jimo remained—was this not roots gone while branches still stood?
translations.idiomatic: When Yue Yi conquered more than seventy Qi cities, only Jimo remained—is that not a tree whose roots are gone but one branch still stands?

sentences.zh: 且夫降順之人，驗之古今，未有不由危逼者。

translations.literal: Moreover, those who surrender, tested through antiquity and the present, have never lacked desperate compulsion.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, throughout history those who surrender have almost always done so under dire pressure.

sentences.zh: 故黃權無路歸款，列地封侯。

translations.literal: Thus Huang Quan, with no road left, returned in allegiance and received enfeoffment as marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Quan had no other path and submitted, and was enfeoffed as marquis.

sentences.zh: 且薛安都、畢眾敬危急投命，並受茅土之爵。

translations.literal: Moreover Xue Andu and Bi Zongjing, in urgent peril throwing themselves on mercy, both received estates and noble titles.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Andu and Bi Zongjing, fleeing in extremity, both received fiefs and noble rank.

sentences.zh: 論古則如彼，語今則如此，明明之世，不及比流。

translations.literal: Speaking of antiquity it was so, speaking of the present likewise—yet in this luminous age they do not reach such a stream.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients did thus and the present should as well—yet in this enlightened age such cases are not matched.

sentences.zh: 竊惟梁鄒嚴固，地據中齊，粟支十載，控弦數千萬，方之升城，不可同日而語。

translations.literal: I consider Liangzou stern and solid, occupying central Qi, with grain to support ten years and archers numbering in the tens of thousands; compared with Shengcheng it cannot be spoken of on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzou was strongly fortified in central Qi, with ten years' grain and thousands of bowmen—Shengcheng was not in the same league.

sentences.zh: 升城猶能抗兵累旬，傷殺甚眾，若臣亡父固守孤城，則非一朝可克。」

translations.literal: Shengcheng could still resist arms for many tens of days and inflict very many casualties; if my late father had held a lone city fast, it would not have fallen in a morning.
translations.idiomatic: Shengcheng held for weeks and cost many lives; had my father stubbornly defended one city, it would not have fallen overnight."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「歷城既陷，梁鄒便是掌中，何煩兵力。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Once Licheng fell, Liangzou was in the palm of the hand—why trouble military force.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Once Licheng fell, Liangzou was already in our grasp—why need more force?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「若如聖旨，白曜便應窮兵極意，取勝俯仰，何為上假赤虎之信，下衒知變之民？」

translations.literal: He replied: "If it were as Your Majesty says, Baiyao should have exhausted arms and will to take victory in a glance—why above borrow Chihu's message and below display knowledge of change to the people?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "If so, Baiyao should have crushed the city at once—why swear by Chihu above and parade promises of mercy below?"

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「卿父此勳，本自至少，以卿才地，豈假殷勤。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your father's merit was originally very slight; with your talent and standing, why need such earnest pleading."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your father's service was slight to begin with; with your gifts and station, why such earnest pleading?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣尩愚六蔽，文武無施，響絕九皐，聞天無日，遭逢聖運，萬死猶生。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your subject is weak and foolish in six obscurations, without achievement in civil or military affairs, his voice lost beyond the nine mounds, without a day of hearing heaven—yet encountering the sage fortune, ten thousand deaths are still life.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I am dull and unaccomplished in civil and military matters, cut off from the court's light—yet under your sage reign even death becomes life.

sentences.zh: 但臣竊見徐兗是賊藩要，徐兗既降，諸戍皆應國有。

translations.literal: Yet your subject observes that Xu and Yan are key to the rebel screen; once Xu and Yan surrendered, all garrisons should belong to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I see that Xu and Yan were vital to the rebel frontier; once they fell, every garrison should have followed.

sentences.zh: 而東徐州刺史張讜所戍團城，領二郡而已。

translations.literal: Yet Eastern Xu Inspector Zhang Zhen garrisoned Tuancheng, holding only two commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhang Zhen, Inspector of Eastern Xu, held Tuancheng with only two commanderies.

sentences.zh: 徐兗降後，猶閉門拒命，授以方嶽，始乃歸降。

translations.literal: After Xu and Yan surrendered he still shut the gates and refused orders; only when given a regional post did he at last submit.
translations.idiomatic: After Xu and Yan submitted he still barred his gates until given a regional post, only then yielding.

sentences.zh: 父子二人，並蒙侯爵。

translations.literal: Father and son both received marquisates.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son were both enfeoffed as marquises.

sentences.zh: 論功比勤，不先臣父。」

translations.literal: Weighing merit and diligence, they were not ahead of my father."
translations.idiomatic: Judged by merit and effort, they were not ahead of my father."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「卿引張讜，讜事小異。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You cite Zhang Zhen; Zhen's case differs slightly."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You cite Zhang Zhen—but his case differs."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣未識異狀。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your subject does not know the differing circumstances."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I do not know the particulars of that difference."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「張讜始來送款，終不差信。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Zhang Zhen from the first came offering allegiance and in the end was never faithless.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Zhang Zhen came offering allegiance from the start and never broke faith.

sentences.zh: 卿父進非先覺，退又拒守，何得不異？」

translations.literal: Your father advanced without foresight and retreated while holding out—how can it not differ?"
translations.idiomatic: Your father neither sensed the moment nor yielded promptly—how can the cases be the same?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「張讜父子，始有歸順之名，後有閉門之罪，以功補過，免罪為幸。

translations.literal: He replied: "Zhang Zhen father and son first had the name of returning to allegiance, later the crime of shutting the gates; to repair fault with merit and escape punishment was already fortune.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "The Zhens first earned a name for submission, then committed the fault of holding out—using merit to offset fault was already lenient.

sentences.zh: 臣又見崔僧祐母弟，隨其叔父道固在歷城。

translations.literal: Your subject also saw Cui Sengyou's mother and younger brother follow their uncle Dao Gu in Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: I also saw Cui Sengyou's mother and brother with their uncle Dao Gu in Licheng.

sentences.zh: 僧祐遙聞王威遠及，恐母弟淪亡，督率鄉閭來欲救援。

translations.literal: Sengyou, hearing from afar of the royal army's distant might, feared his kin would perish and led his township to come intending rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the imperial army's approach, Sengyou feared for his kin and led his township to rescue them.

sentences.zh: 既至郁洲，歷城已沒，束手歸誠，救母弟之命。

translations.literal: When he reached Yuzhou Licheng had already fallen; with empty hands he returned in sincerity, saving his mother and brother's lives.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Yuzhou too late; Licheng had fallen, and he submitted empty-handed to save his family.

sentences.zh: 聖朝嘉其附化，賞以三品。

translations.literal: The sage court commended his coming over and rewarded him with third rank.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his submission and rewarded him with third rank.

sentences.zh: 亡父之誠，豈後僧祐？」

translations.literal: My late father's sincerity—how could it come after Sengyou?"
translations.idiomatic: How could my father's loyalty rank below Sengyou's?"

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「僧祐身居東海，去留任意，來則有位，去則他人，是故賞之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Sengyou's person was in Donghai; coming and going were at his will—come and he had a post, go and he belonged to others; therefore he was rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Sengyou lived in Donghai and could come or go freely—arrive and receive office, leave and belong elsewhere; that is why he was rewarded.

sentences.zh: 卿父被圍孤城，已是己物，所以不賞。」

translations.literal: Your father was besieged in a lone city and was already our possession; therefore he was not rewarded."
translations.idiomatic: Your father was trapped in a lone city already within our grasp; that is why he was not rewarded."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「亡父據城歸國，至公也；

translations.literal: He replied: "My late father held the city and returned to the state—this was utmost fairness;
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "My father held the city and submitted to the state—that was public duty;

sentences.zh: 僧祐意計而來，為私也。

translations.literal: Sengyou came by calculation—this was private.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyou came by private calculation.

sentences.zh: 為私蒙賞，至公不酬，臣未見其可。」

translations.literal: Private action receives reward, utmost fairness goes unrewarded—your subject has not seen how that can be right."
translations.idiomatic: Private motives win reward while public duty goes unpaid—I do not see how that is just."

sentences.zh: 高祖笑而不言。

translations.literal: The emperor smiled and said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor smiled and said no more.

sentences.zh: 比部尚書陸叡叱文曄曰：「假令先朝謬賞僧祐，豈可謬相賞也！」

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Lu Rui rebuked Wenye: "Suppose the former court mistakenly rewarded Sengyou—can one mistakenly reward you too!"
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Lu Rui rebuked Wenye, "If the former court erred in rewarding Sengyou, must we err again in rewarding you?"

sentences.zh: 文曄曰：「先帝中代聖主，與日月等曜，比隆堯舜，宰相則十亂五臣，今言謬賞，豈不仰誣先朝乎？」

translations.literal: Wenye said: "The former emperor was a sage of the middle generation, equal in brightness to sun and moon, comparable to Yao and Shun; his ministers were the ten chaotic and five ministerial—now to speak of mistaken reward, is that not slandering the former court?"
translations.idiomatic: Wenye said, "The late emperor was a sage comparable to Yao and Shun; to call his rewards mistaken is to slander him."

sentences.zh: 尚書高閭曰：「卿謂母弟與妻子何者為重？」

translations.literal: Minister Gao Lu said: "Do you hold mother and younger brother or wife and children the heavier?"
translations.idiomatic: Minister Gao Lu asked, "Which weighs heavier for you—mother and brother, or wife and children?"

sentences.zh: 文曄曰：「母弟為重。」

translations.literal: Wenye said: "Mother and younger brother are heavier."
translations.idiomatic: Wenye said, "Mother and brother weigh heavier."

sentences.zh: 閭曰：「卿知母弟為重，朝廷賞僧祐是也。

translations.literal: Lu said: "You know mother and younger brother are heavier; the court's reward of Sengyou is right.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu said, "You admit mother and brother matter more; the court was right to reward Sengyou.

sentences.zh: 卿父為妻子而來，事何相反？」

translations.literal: Your father came for wife and children—the matter is quite the opposite?"
translations.idiomatic: Your father came for his wife and children—the cases are opposite, are they not?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「僧祐若無母弟，來歸以不？」

translations.literal: He replied: "If Sengyou had no mother and younger brother, would he have come to allegiance or not?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked, "If Sengyou had no mother and brother, would he still have come?"

sentences.zh: 閭曰：「不來。」

translations.literal: Lu said: "He would not have come."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu said, "He would not."

sentences.zh: 文曄曰：「若僧祐赴母弟之難，此是其私。

translations.literal: Wenye said: "If Sengyou went to his mother and brother's distress, that was his private feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Wenye said, "If Sengyou came for his family's distress, that was private feeling.

sentences.zh: 而亡父本為大丈夫，立身處世，豈可顧妻子而虧高節也！

translations.literal: Yet my late father was fundamentally a great man in establishing himself in the world—how could he look to wife and children and impair high integrity!
translations.idiomatic: My father was a man of standing—how could he trade honor for his family!

sentences.zh: 昔樂羊食子，有顧以不？

translations.literal: Formerly Yue Yi ate his son—did he look back or not?
translations.idiomatic: When Yue Yi ate his son, did he look back?

sentences.zh: 亡父本心，實不垂顧，所以歸化者，自知商周不敵，天命有所歸。」

translations.literal: My late father's true heart in fact did not look back; therefore he submitted, knowing Shang and Zhou could not be matched and that Heaven's mandate had its destination."
translations.idiomatic: My father's true heart did not waver; he submitted knowing he could not resist and that Heaven had chosen."

sentences.zh: 高祖謂文曄曰：「卿之所訴，[4]頗亦有途。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Wenye: "What you plead [4] also has some ground.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Wenye, "Your plea [4] has some merit.

sentences.zh: 賞從重，罰從輕，尋敕酬敍。」

translations.literal: Rewards follow weight, punishments follow lightness; I shall soon order compensation.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards should be generous and punishments light; I shall order due compensation."

sentences.zh: 文曄泣曰：「臣愚頓理極，再見無期，陛下既垂慈澤，願敕有司，特賜矜理。」

translations.literal: Wenye wept and said: "Your subject's foolishness has reached the limit; to see you again has no term; Your Majesty having shown gracious favor, I beg the authorities specially to show pity in judgment."
translations.idiomatic: Wenye wept, "I am at my wit's end; I may never see you again—yet if Your Majesty shows mercy, I beg the officials to judge me with compassion."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「王者無戲，何待懃懃。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "A king has no jest—why wait so earnestly?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "A ruler does not jest—why plead so urgently?"

sentences.zh: 既而賜文曄爵都昌子，深見待遇。

translations.literal: Soon he enfeoffed Wenye as Viscount of Duchang and showed him deep favor.
translations.idiomatic: He soon enfeoffed Wenye as Viscount of Duchang and treated him with marked favor.

sentences.zh: 拜協律中郎，[5]改授羽林監。

translations.literal: He was appointed Harmonizer-in-Chief, [5] then transferred to Supervisor of the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Harmonizer-in-Chief, [5] then made Supervisor of the Feathered Forest.

sentences.zh: 世宗世，除高陽太守。

translations.literal: In Emperor Shizong's time he was made Administrator of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizong he served as Administrator of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 延昌中卒。

translations.literal: He died in the Yanxing era.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Yanchang reign.

sentences.zh: 贈平遠將軍、光州刺史，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the Distance and Inspector of Guang, with posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance and Inspector of Guang, with the posthumous name Zhen.

sentences.zh: 子元，襲。

translations.literal: His son Yuan inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 拜員外郎、襄威將軍、青州別駕。

translations.literal: He was appointed Outer Palace Gentleman, General of Majestic Might, and Vice-Prefect of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Outer Palace Gentleman, General of Majestic Might, and Vice-Prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 文顥，性仁孝篤厚。

translations.literal: Wenhao was by nature humane, filial, and sincere.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhao was humane, filial, and deeply sincere by nature.

sentences.zh: 徐州安豐王府騎兵參軍。

translations.literal: Cavalry Commandant in the household of the Prince of Anfeng of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was Cavalry Commandant in the household of the Prince of Anfeng of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 季友，南青州左軍府錄事參軍。

translations.literal: Jiyou was Recorder in the Left Army office of Southern Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyou served as recorder in the Left Army staff of Southern Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 聞慰，博識有才思。

translations.literal: Wen Wei was broadly learned and had talent and thought.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Wei was learned and resourceful.

sentences.zh: 至延興中，南叛。

translations.literal: By the Yanxing era he rebelled southward.
translations.idiomatic: By the Yanxing era he had defected south.

sentences.zh: 休賓叔父旋之，其妻許氏，二子法鳳、法武。

translations.literal: Xiubin's uncle by marriage Xuanzhi had wife Lady Xu and two sons Fafeng and Fawu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiubin's uncle by marriage Xuanzhi left Lady Xu and sons Fafeng and Fawu.

sentences.zh: [6]而旋之早亡。

translations.literal: [6] Yet Xuanzhi had died early.
translations.idiomatic: [6] Xuanzhi had died young.

sentences.zh: 東陽平，許氏攜二子入國，孤貧不自立，並疏薄不倫，為時人所棄。

translations.literal: When Dongyang was pacified, Lady Xu brought the two sons into the state; impoverished and unable to support themselves, they were all negligent and unseemly and were abandoned by men of the time.
translations.idiomatic: When Dongyang fell, Lady Xu brought the sons north; destitute and dissolute, they were scorned by respectable society.

sentences.zh: 母子皆出家為尼，[7]既而反俗。

translations.literal: Mother and sons all left home to become nuns; [7] later they returned to lay life.
translations.idiomatic: Mother and sons took monastic vows; [7] later they returned to lay life.

sentences.zh: 太和中，高祖選盡物望，河南人士，才學之徒，咸見申擢。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era Emperor Gaozu selected men of the highest reputation; scholars and men of talent from Henan were all promoted.
translations.idiomatic: During Taihe the emperor promoted men of the highest reputation, and talented scholars from Henan were elevated.

sentences.zh: 法鳳兄弟無可收用，不蒙選授。

translations.literal: The Fafeng brothers had nothing by which they could be employed and received no appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The Fafeng brothers were deemed unfit and received no appointment.

sentences.zh: 後俱奔南。

translations.literal: Later both fled south.
translations.idiomatic: Later both fled south.

sentences.zh: 法武後改名孝標云。

translations.literal: Fawu later changed his name to Xiaobiao.
translations.idiomatic: Fawu later took the name Xiaobiao.

sentences.zh: 房法壽，小名烏頭，清河繹幕人也。

translations.literal: Fang Fashou, childhood name Wutou, was a native of Yimo in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Fashou, childhood name Wutou, came from Yimo in Qinghe Commandery.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，少好射獵，輕率勇果，結群小而為劫盜。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, from youth he loved shooting and hunting, was light and brave, and banded with petty men to rob.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he loved hunting and was reckless and bold, leading a band of robbers.

sentences.zh: 從叔元慶、範鎮等坐法壽被州郡切責，時月相繼，宗族甚患之。

translations.literal: His cousins Yuanqing, Fanzhen, and others because of Fashou were sternly pursued by the province and prefecture month after month; the clan was greatly troubled.
translations.idiomatic: His cousins Yuanqing and Fanzhen suffered repeated prosecution because of him, to the clan's great distress.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，州迎主簿。

translations.literal: At twenty he was welcomed as chief clerk of the province.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he was invited to serve as the province's chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 後以母老，不復應州郡之命。

translations.literal: Later because his mother was old he no longer answered provincial and prefectural orders.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother grew old he refused further provincial appointments.

sentences.zh: 常盜殺猪牛，以共其母。

translations.literal: He often stole pigs and cattle to supply his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He often stole livestock to feed his mother.

sentences.zh: 招集壯士，常有百數。

translations.literal: He gathered stalwart men and regularly had several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered fighting men and usually commanded several hundred.

sentences.zh: 母亡歲餘，遇沈文秀、崔道固起兵應劉子勛。

translations.literal: More than a year after his mother's death he encountered Shen Wenxiu and Cui Daogu raising troops in response to Liu Zixun.
translations.idiomatic: A year after his mother's death, Shen Wenxiu and Cui Daogu rose for Liu Zixun.

sentences.zh: 明僧暠、劉乘民起兵應劉彧，攻討文秀。

translations.literal: Ming Sengao and Liu Chenmin raised troops in response to Liu Yu and attacked Wenxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Sengao and Liu Chenmin rose for Liu Yu and attacked Wenxiu.

sentences.zh: 法壽亦與清河太守王玄邈起兵西屯，合討道固。

translations.literal: Fashou also with Administrator of Qinghe Wang Xuanmiao raised troops and encamped west, joining to attack Daogu.
translations.idiomatic: Fashou joined Qinghe Administrator Wang Xuanmiao in a western camp to attack Daogu.

sentences.zh: 玄邈以法壽為司馬，累破道固軍，甚為歷城所憚。

translations.literal: Xuanmiao made Fashou Chief Commandant; repeatedly defeating Daogu's army, he was greatly feared by Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmiao made him chief of staff; he repeatedly defeated Daogu and was greatly feared at Licheng.

sentences.zh: 加法壽綏邊將軍、魏郡太守。

translations.literal: Fashou was added as General Who Pacifies the Frontier and Administrator of Wei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General Who Pacifies the Frontier and Administrator of Wei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 子勛死，道固、文秀悉復歸彧，乃罷兵。

translations.literal: When Zixun died, Daogu and Wenxiu all returned to Yu and the armies were disbanded.
translations.idiomatic: When Zixun died, Daogu and Wenxiu submitted to Yu and the armies dispersed.

sentences.zh: 道固慮其扇亂百姓，遂切遣之。

translations.literal: Daogu feared he would incite the people to disorder and urgently sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Daogu feared he would stir the populace and ordered him away at once.

sentences.zh: 而法壽外託裝辦而內不欲行。

translations.literal: Yet Fashou outwardly claimed to prepare baggage while inwardly he did not wish to go.
translations.idiomatic: Fashou pretended to pack for departure but inwardly refused to leave.

sentences.zh: 會從弟崇吉在升城，為慕容白曜所破，母妻沒於白曜軍。

translations.literal: It happened that his cousin Chongji was in Shengcheng when Murong Baiyao broke it; mother and wife were taken in Baiyao's army.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Chongji was in Shengcheng when Baiyao took it; Fashou's mother and wife fell captive.

sentences.zh: 崇吉奔還舊宅。

translations.literal: Chongji fled back to the old residence.
translations.idiomatic: Chongji fled home.

sentences.zh: 法壽與崇吉年志粗相諧協，而親則從祖兄弟也。

translations.literal: Fashou and Chongji were roughly alike in age and aspiration, and by kinship were cousins from the same grandfather.
