translations.idiomatic: Fashou and Chongji were close in age and temperament and were first cousins.

sentences.zh: 崇吉以母妻見獲，託法壽為計。

translations.literal: Chongji because mother and wife were captured entrusted Fashou with a plan.
translations.idiomatic: Chongji, with his family captive, asked Fashou for a plan.

sentences.zh: 法壽既不欲南行，恨道固逼切，又矜崇吉情理。

translations.literal: Fashou, not wishing to go south, hated Daogu's pressure, and also pitied Chongji's situation.
translations.idiomatic: Fashou, unwilling to go south, resented Daogu's pressure and pitied Chongji.

sentences.zh: 時道固以兼治中房靈賓督清河、廣川郡事，戍盤陽。

translations.literal: At that time Daogu because of concurrent service had Fang Lingbin of the Secretariat supervise Qinghe and Guangchuan and garrison Panyang.
translations.idiomatic: Daogu had Fang Lingbin of the Secretariat hold Qinghe and Guangchuan and garrison Panyang.

sentences.zh: 法壽遂與崇吉潛謀襲靈賓，克之。

translations.literal: Fashou then with Chongji secretly plotted to strike Lingbin and took him.
translations.idiomatic: Fashou and Chongji secretly attacked Lingbin and seized Panyang.

sentences.zh: 仍歸款於白曜以贖母妻。

translations.literal: He then returned in allegiance to Baiyao to ransom mother and wife.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted to Baiyao to ransom his family.

sentences.zh: 白曜遣將軍長孫觀等自大山南入馬耳關以赴盤陽，還崇吉母妻。

translations.literal: Baiyao sent General Zhangsun Guan and others from south of Great Mountain into Ma'er Pass toward Panyang and returned Chongji's mother and wife.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao sent Zhangsun Guan through Ma'er Pass to Panyang and restored Chongji's family.

sentences.zh: 初，道固遣軍圍盤陽，法壽等拒守二十餘日。

translations.literal: Earlier Daogu had sent troops to besiege Panyang; Fashou and others held out more than twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: Daogu had besieged Panyang for over twenty days.

sentences.zh: 觀軍至，賊乃散走。

translations.literal: When Guan's army arrived the bandits scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Guan's troops arrived the enemy scattered.

sentences.zh: 觀軍入城，詔以法壽為平遠將軍，與韓騏驎對為冀州刺史，督上租糧。

translations.literal: When Guan's army entered the city, an edict appointed Fashou General Who Pacifies the Distance, paired with Han Qilin as Inspector of Ji to supervise upper tax grain.
translations.idiomatic: Guan entered the city and Fashou was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance, paired with Han Qilin as Inspector of Ji to collect grain taxes.

sentences.zh: 以法壽從父弟靈民為清河太守，思順為濟南太守，靈悅為平原太守，伯憐為廣川太守，叔玉為高陽太守，叔玉兄伯玉為河間太守，伯玉從父弟思安為樂陵太守，思安弟幼安為高密太守，以安初附。

translations.literal: Fashou's cousins Lingmin, Sishun, Lingyue, Bolian, Shuyu, Shuyu's elder brother Boyu, Boyu's cousin Si'an, and Si'an's younger brother You'an were made administrators of Qinghe, Jinan, Pingyuan, Guangchuan, Gaoyang, Hejian, Leling, and Gaomi respectively, because they had first submitted.
translations.idiomatic: A host of Fang cousins received prefectural posts across the region for their early submission.

sentences.zh: 及歷城、梁鄒降，法壽、崇吉等與崔道固、劉休賓俱至京師。

translations.literal: When Licheng and Liangzou surrendered, Fashou, Chongji, and others with Cui Daogu and Liu Xiubin all reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Licheng and Liangzou fell, Fashou, Chongji, Daogu, and Xiubin all came to the capital.

sentences.zh: 以法壽為上客，崇吉為次客，崔劉為下客。

translations.literal: Fashou was made chief guest, Chongji second guest, Cui and Liu lower guests.
translations.idiomatic: Fashou was received as chief guest, Chongji as second guest, Cui and Liu as lower guests.

sentences.zh: 法壽供給，亞於安都等。

translations.literal: Fashou's provisions were second only to Andu and the like.
translations.idiomatic: His stipend ranked just below men like Bi Zongjing.

sentences.zh: 以功賜爵壯武侯，加平遠將軍，[8]給以田宅、奴婢。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhuangwu and added General Who Pacifies the Distance, [8] given fields, houses, slaves, and servants.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Zhuangwu, given further rank, [8] and granted estates, slaves, and servants.

sentences.zh: 性好酒，愛施，親舊賓客率同飢飽，坎壈常不豐足。

translations.literal: He loved wine by nature and loved giving; kin, old friends, and guests all ate hunger and fullness alike, and he was often not abundantly supplied.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine and generosity; kin and guests shared feast or famine alike, and he was often short of means.

sentences.zh: 畢眾敬等皆尚其通愛。

translations.literal: Bi Zongjing and others all admired his open affection.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Zongjing and others admired his open-handed warmth.

sentences.zh: 太和中卒。

translations.literal: He died in the Taihe era.
translations.idiomatic: He died during Taihe.

sentences.zh: 贈平東將軍、青州刺史，諡敬侯。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Qing, with posthumous title Marquis Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Qing, with the posthumous name Marquis Jing.

sentences.zh: 子伯祖，襲，例降為伯。

translations.literal: His son Bozu inherited; by precedent the title was reduced to earl.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bozu succeeded; by precedent the rank was reduced to earl.

sentences.zh: 歷齊郡內史。

translations.literal: He served as inner administrator of Qi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He served as inner administrator of Qi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 伯祖闇弱，委事於功曹張僧皓，僧皓大有受納，伯祖衣食不充。

translations.literal: Bozu was dim and weak and entrusted affairs to Merit Officer Zhang Senghao; Senghao took many bribes and Bozu lacked food and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Bozu was weak and left affairs to Zhang Senghao, who took heavy bribes while Bozu went wanting.

sentences.zh: 後廣陵王羽為青州，伯祖為從事中郎、平原相。

translations.literal: Later when Prince Yu of Guangling was in Qingzhou, Bozu was Attendant of the Masters of Writing and Administrator of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Prince Yu of Guangling governed Qingzhou, Bozu served on his staff and as Administrator of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 轉幽州輔國長史，坐公事免官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Clerk in the Rear Army of Youzhou's General Who Supports the State and was dismissed for public-office fault.
translations.idiomatic: He became chief clerk in the Youzhou rear army staff, then was dismissed for an official offense.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子翼，襲。

translations.literal: His son Yi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 宣威將軍、大城戍主。

translations.literal: General of Manifest Might and commander of the Dacheng garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was General of Manifest Might and commander of the Dacheng garrison.

sentences.zh: 永安中，青州太傅開府從事中郎。

translations.literal: In the Yong'an era he was Attendant of the Masters of Writing in the Grand Tutor's Qingzhou headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: During Yong'an he served on the Grand Tutor's Qingzhou staff.

sentences.zh: 伯祖弟叔祖，別以功賜爵魏昌子。

translations.literal: Bozu's younger brother Shuzu separately received enfeoffment as Viscount of Weichang for merit.
translations.idiomatic: Bozu's younger brother Shuzu was separately enfeoffed Viscount of Weichang for merit.

sentences.zh: 歷廣陵王國郎中令、長廣東萊二郡太守、龍驤將軍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: He served as Director of the Masters of Writing in the Prince of Guangling's kingdom, Administrator of the two commanderies of Changguang and Donglai, General of the Dragon Cavalry, and Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was director of the masters of writing for Prince of Guangling, administered Changguang and Donglai, and held general and palace posts.

sentences.zh: 永安中，安東將軍、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Yong'an era he was General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: During Yong'an he was General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Ying.

sentences.zh: 叔祖弟幼愍，安豐、新蔡二郡太守。

translations.literal: Shuzu's younger brother Youmin was Administrator of the two commanderies of Anfeng and Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzu's younger brother Youmin administered Anfeng and Xincai.

sentences.zh: 坐事奪官，居家，忽聞有客聲，出無所見，還至庭中，為家群犬所噬，遂卒。

translations.literal: He was stripped of office for an offense and lived at home; suddenly hearing guests' voices he went out and saw no one; returning to the courtyard he was torn by the household dogs and died.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of office, he was at home when he heard visitors, found no one outside, and was killed by the household dogs in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 初，長孫觀之將至盤陽也，城中稍以震懼。

translations.literal: When Zhangsun Guan was about to reach Panyang the city was somewhat shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhangsun Guan approached Panyang the garrison grew fearful.

sentences.zh: 時劉彧給事中崔平仲欲歸江南，自歷下至圍城軍中，與十餘騎遙共法壽語，靈賓密遣人捕執之。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Yu's attendant Cui Pingzhong wished to return to Jiangnan; from Licheng down to the besieging army he spoke from afar with Fashou with more than ten horsemen; Lingbin secretly sent men to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu's attendant Cui Pingzhong tried to flee south and spoke with Fashou outside the walls; Lingbin had him seized.

sentences.zh: 始法壽克盤陽之後，常禁靈賓於別齋。

translations.literal: From the first after Fashou took Panyang he regularly confined Lingbin in a separate lodge.
translations.idiomatic: After taking Panyang Fashou kept Lingbin under house arrest.

sentences.zh: 既得平仲，引與同室，致酒食，敍國軍明將入意。

translations.literal: Having obtained Pingzhong he led him to the same room, set out wine and food, and explained that the state army's enlightened generals would enter.
translations.idiomatic: Once Pingzhong was captured, Fashou feasted him and explained the imperial army's imminent entry.

sentences.zh: 夜中，北城上縋出平仲、靈賓等十餘人。

translations.literal: In the night on the north wall they lowered Pingzhong, Lingbin, and more than ten others by rope.
translations.idiomatic: That night they lowered Pingzhong, Lingbin, and a dozen others over the north wall.

sentences.zh: 厥明，官軍至城，靈賓遂歸梁鄒。

translations.literal: At dawn when the official army reached the city Lingbin returned to Liangzou.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the imperial troops arrived and Lingbin fled to Liangzou.

sentences.zh: 靈賓，文藻不如兄靈建，而辯悟過之。

translations.literal: Lingbin's literary ornament was not equal to his elder brother Lingjian's, but in quick wit he surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: Lingbin was less literary than his brother Lingjian but quicker in debate.

sentences.zh: 靈建在南，官至州治中、勃海太守，以才名見稱。

translations.literal: Lingjian in the south reached Chief Clerk of the province and Administrator of Bohai and was famed for talent.
translations.idiomatic: Lingjian in the south rose to provincial chief clerk and Administrator of Bohai, famed for talent.

sentences.zh: 兄弟俱入國，為平齊民。

translations.literal: The brothers both entered the state and became Pingqi people.
translations.idiomatic: Both brothers came north and became Pingqi subjects.

sentences.zh: 雖流漂屯圮，操尚卓然。

translations.literal: Though drifting in ruin and hardship, their conduct remained lofty.
translations.idiomatic: Though displaced and ruined, they kept their integrity.

sentences.zh: 並卒於平齊。

translations.literal: Both died in Pingqi.
translations.idiomatic: Both died in Pingqi.

sentences.zh: 靈建子宣明，亦文學著稱，雅有父風。

translations.literal: Lingjian's son Xuanming was also famed in letters and elegantly had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Lingjian's son Xuanming was also literary and resembled his father.

sentences.zh: 高祖擢為中書博士。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu promoted him as Erudite of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu made him an erudite of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遷洛，轉議郎，試守東清河郡。

translations.literal: When the capital moved to Luoyang he was transferred to Reviewer and tried as acting Administrator of Eastern Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: After the move to Luoyang he became a reviewer and acting Administrator of Eastern Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 正始中，京兆王愉出除征東、冀州，以宣明為記室參軍。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi era Prince Jingzhao Yu went out as General Who Conquers the East of Ji and made Xuanming his recorder.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengshi, Prince Yu of Jingzhao went east as commander of Ji and made Xuanming his recorder.

sentences.zh: 愉反，逼宣明為太守。

translations.literal: When Yu rebelled he forced Xuanming to serve as administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu rebelled he forced Xuanming to serve as administrator.

translations.literal: [9] (Text lost in transmission.)
translations.idiomatic: [9] Text is missing here; after Yuan Yu forced Xuanming to serve as administrator, the account breaks off in the received text.

sentences.zh: 靈賓從父弟堅，字千秋，少有才名。

translations.literal: Lingbin's cousin Jian, courtesy name Qianqiu, from youth had talent and name.
translations.idiomatic: Lingbin's cousin Jian, courtesy name Qianqiu, was talented and famed from youth.

sentences.zh: 亦內徙為平齊民。

translations.literal: He also moved inward and became a Pingqi person.
translations.idiomatic: He too was resettled as a Pingqi subject.

sentences.zh: 太和初，高祖擢為祕書郎，遷司空諮議、齊州大中正。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe Emperor Gaozu promoted him as Secretary Gentleman, then transferred to Consultant of the Minister of Works and Chief Rectifier of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taihe he was made secretary gentleman, then consultant to the Minister of Works and chief rectifier of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 高祖臨朝，令諸州中正各舉所知，千秋與幽州中正陽尼各舉其子。

translations.literal: When the emperor held court he ordered each province's chief rectifiers to recommend those they knew; Qianqiu and Yang Ni, chief rectifier of Youzhou, each recommended their sons.
translations.idiomatic: At court the emperor ordered chief rectifiers to recommend talent; Qianqiu and Youzhou's Yang Ni each nominated their sons.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「昔有一祁，名垂往史，今有二奚，當聞來牒。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Formerly there was one Qi and his name hangs on past records; now there are two Xi and they should be heard of in future registers."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Once one Qi made history; now two Xis should do the same."

sentences.zh: 出為濮陽太守。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted Administrator of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，復為司空諮議，加立忠將軍。

translations.literal: In Emperor Shizong's time he again became Consultant of the Minister of Works and was added General Who Establishes Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizong he again consulted for the Minister of Works and was made General Who Establishes Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈南青州刺史，諡曰懿。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Inspector of Southern Qing with posthumous title Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Inspector of Southern Qing with the posthumous name Yi.

sentences.zh: 長子祖淵，羽林監。

translations.literal: His eldest son Zuyuan was Supervisor of the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Zuyuan was Supervisor of the Feathered Forest.

sentences.zh: 從章武王融討葛榮，沒於陳。

translations.literal: Following Prince Rong of Zhangwu in the campaign against Ge Rong he perished in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Following Prince Rong of Zhangwu against Ge Rong he fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 贈安東將軍、濟州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Ji.

sentences.zh: 祖淵弟祖皓，長水校尉。

translations.literal: Zuyuan's younger brother Zuhao was Colonel Director of the Long River.
translations.idiomatic: Zuyuan's younger brother Zuhao was Colonel Director of the Long River.

sentences.zh: 後討蕭衍將於九山，戰歿。

translations.literal: Later campaigning against a general of Xiao Yan at Jiushan he died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Later, fighting a Liang general at Jiushan, he died in battle.

sentences.zh: 贈撫軍將軍、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Yan.

sentences.zh: 崔平仲自東陽南奔，妻子於歷城入國。

translations.literal: Cui Pingzhong fled south from Dongyang; wife and children entered the state from Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Pingzhong fled south from Dongyang while his family entered the north from Licheng.

sentences.zh: 太和中，高祖聽其還南。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era Emperor Gaozu permitted his return south.
translations.idiomatic: During Taihe the emperor allowed his return south.

sentences.zh: 思安，有勇力；

translations.literal: Si'an had martial strength;
translations.idiomatic: Si'an was strong and brave;

sentences.zh: 伯玉，果敢有將略。

translations.literal: Boyu was bold and had general's strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Boyu was bold and strategically gifted.

sentences.zh: 思安賜爵西安子、建威將軍、北平太守，遷大司馬司馬、齊州武昌王府司馬。

translations.literal: Si'an was enfeoffed Viscount of Xi'an, made General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Beiping, then moved to Chief Clerk in the Grand Marshal's office and Chief Clerk in Prince Wuchang of Qi's household in Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Si'an was enfeoffed Viscount of Xi'an, made General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Beiping, then served on the Grand Marshal's and Prince of Qi's staffs in Qi.

sentences.zh: 高祖南伐，徵為步兵校尉、直閤將軍、中統軍。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned south he was summoned as Colonel Director of Footsoldiers, Direct Attendant General, and Central Army Commander.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern campaign he was summoned as colonel of footsoldiers, direct attendant general, and central army commander.

sentences.zh: 善撫士眾，高祖嘉之。

translations.literal: He was good at comforting troops and the emperor commended him.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at rallying troops and won the emperor's praise.

sentences.zh: 漢陽既平，復為武昌王司馬，帶東魏郡太守，加寧朔將軍，改爵清河子，卒官。

translations.literal: After Hanyang was pacified he again became chief clerk to Prince Wuchang and concurrently Administrator of Eastern Wei Commandery, added General Who Pacifies the North, changed enfeoffment to Viscount of Qinghe, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: After Hanyang fell he again served Prince Wuchang, governed Eastern Wei, was made General Who Pacifies the North, enfeoffed Viscount of Qinghe, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子敬寶襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Jingbao inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingbao succeeded.

sentences.zh: 敬寶，亦壯健。

translations.literal: Jingbao was also sturdy.
translations.idiomatic: Jingbao was also robust.

sentences.zh: 奉朝請、征北中兵參軍、北征統軍、寧遠將軍，每有戰功。

translations.literal: Gentleman at Court, staff officer in the Army of the North, commander of the northern expedition, General Who Pacifies the Distance—each campaign brought merit.
translations.idiomatic: He served at court and on northern campaigns as staff officer and commander, winning merit in every fight.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 子去病襲。

translations.literal: His son Qubing inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qubing succeeded.

sentences.zh: 伯玉，坐弟叔玉南奔，徙於北邊。

translations.literal: Boyu, because his younger brother Shuyu fled south, was relocated to the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Boyu was banished north because his brother Shuyu defected south.

sentences.zh: 後亦南叛，為蕭鸞南陽太守。

translations.literal: Later he too rebelled south and became Xiao Luan's Administrator of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He later defected south and became Xiao Luan's Administrator of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖南伐，克宛外城，命舍人公孫延景宣詔於伯玉曰：「天無二日，土無兩王，是以躬總六師，蕩一四海。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned south and took the outer wall of Wan, he ordered Attendant Gongsun Yanjing to proclaim an edict to Boyu: "Heaven has no second sun, earth no second king; therefore I personally lead the six armies to pacify the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took Wan's outer walls, he had Gongsun Yanjing proclaim to Boyu, "Heaven admits no second sun— I lead the six armies to pacify the realm.

sentences.zh: 宛城小戍，豈足以禦抗王威？

translations.literal: This small garrison—how can it resist royal might?
translations.idiomatic: How can this little fortress resist imperial might?

sentences.zh: 深可三思，封侯胙土，事在俯仰。」

translations.literal: Think deeply; enfeoffment and fief depend on a single bow.
translations.idiomatic: Think carefully—titles and fiefs hang on your next move."

sentences.zh: 伯玉對曰：「外臣荷國厚恩，奉任疆境，為臣之道，未敢聽命。

translations.literal: Boyu replied: "Your outer subject bears the state's thick grace and holds a frontier post; as a minister's way, I dare not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Boyu replied, "I owe the state deep grace and hold the frontier; as a minister I dare not obey.

sentences.zh: 伏惟遊鑾遠涉，願不損神。」

translations.literal: I respectfully hope Your touring chariot, crossing far, will not harm your spirit."
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty's distant march will not tax your health."

sentences.zh: 高祖又遣謂曰：「朕親率麾斾，遠清江沔，此之小戍，豈足徘徊王師。

translations.literal: The emperor again sent word: "I personally lead the banners far to clear the Jiang and Han; this small garrison is not worth detaining the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote again, "I have come far to clear the Yangzi and Han— this petty post is not worth detaining the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 但戎輅所經，纖介須殄，宜量力三思，自求多褔。

translations.literal: Yet wherever the war chariot passes, the slightest resistance must be destroyed; you should measure strength and think thrice, seeking your own greater blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever my army passes, resistance will be crushed— measure your strength and choose wisely.

sentences.zh: 且卿早蒙蕭賾殊常之眷，曾不懷恩，報以塵露。

translations.literal: Moreover you early received Xiao Ze's extraordinary favor and did not repay it with dust and dew.
translations.idiomatic: You enjoyed Xiao Ze's special favor yet repaid it with nothing.

sentences.zh: 蕭鸞妄言入繼道成，賾子無孑遺。

translations.literal: Xiao Luan falsely claimed succession from Daocheng; Ze's sons left no descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Luan usurped the throne while Ze's line was extinguished.

sentences.zh: 卿不能建忠於前君，方立節於逆豎，卿之罪一。

translations.literal: You could not build loyalty to the former lord yet now set up integrity toward a rebellious minion—your first crime.
translations.idiomatic: You failed your former lord yet serve a usurper— that is your first crime.

sentences.zh: 又頃年傷我偏師，卿之罪二。

translations.literal: Moreover in recent years you harmed our detached forces—your second crime.
translations.idiomatic: You have harmed our armies— your second crime.

sentences.zh: 今鑾斾親戎，清一南服，不先面縛，待罪麾下，卿之罪三。

translations.literal: Now the imperial chariot campaigns in person to pacify the south; if you do not first come out bound, awaiting punishment under the banners—your third crime.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not bind yourself and submit before my banners— that is your third crime.

sentences.zh: 卿之此戍，多則一年，中則百日，少則三旬，克殄豈遠。

translations.literal: This garrison of yours—at most a year, in the middle a hundred days, at least thirty days—its destruction is not far.
translations.idiomatic: This fortress will fall within a year, a hundred days, or thirty— choose before it is too late.

sentences.zh: 宜善思之，後悔無及。」

translations.literal: Think well; regret will be of no avail."
translations.idiomatic: Think well— regret will come too late."

sentences.zh: 伯玉對曰：「昔蒙武帝愷悌之恩，忝侍左右，此之厚遇，無忘夙夜。

translations.literal: Boyu replied: "Formerly I received Emperor Wu's kind favor and was shamed to attend at his side; this thick treatment I have not forgotten day or night.
translations.idiomatic: Boyu answered, "I received Emperor Wu's kindness at court and have not forgotten it night or day.

sentences.zh: 但繼主失德，民望有歸。

translations.literal: Yet the succeeding lord lost virtue and the people's hope had a destination.
translations.idiomatic: The successor lost virtue and the people's hope turned elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 主上龍飛踐極，光紹大宗，非直副億兆之深望，實兼武皇之遺敕。

translations.literal: Our lord ascended the throne, continuing the great lineage—not only answering the deep hope of the hundred million, but also fulfilling Martial Emperor's testament.
translations.idiomatic: Our present lord ascended legitimately, fulfilling both the people's hope and the late emperor's will.

sentences.zh: 是以懃懃懇懇，不敢失墜。

translations.literal: Therefore earnestly, earnestly, I dare not fail.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I serve earnestly and dare not falter.

sentences.zh: 往者，北師深入，寇擾邊民，輒厲將士，以救蒼生。

translations.literal: Formerly when the northern army went deep and disturbed border people, I then encouraged generals to save the black-haired masses.
translations.idiomatic: When northern armies raided the frontier I rallied troops to protect the people.

sentences.zh: 此乃邊戍常事，陛下不得垂責。」

translations.literal: This is the border garrison's constant affair; Your Majesty must not lay blame on me."
translations.idiomatic: That was a garrison's ordinary duty— Your Majesty should not blame me for it."

sentences.zh: 及克宛，伯玉面縛而降。

translations.literal: When Wan was taken Boyu came out bound to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Wan fell Boyu came out bound in surrender.

sentences.zh: 高祖引見伯玉并其參佐二百人，詔伯玉曰：「朕承天馭宇，方欲清一寰域，卿蕞爾小戍，敢拒六師，卿之愆罪，理在不赦。」

translations.literal: The emperor led Boyu and his staff of two hundred men in audience and said to Boyu: "I receive Heaven and drive the realm, intending to pacify the whole universe; you, a tiny garrison, dared resist the six armies—your fault and crime by principle should not be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received Boyu and two hundred staff and said, "I rule under Heaven and mean to pacify all lands; you dared resist the six armies— by rights you should not be pardoned."

sentences.zh: 伯玉對曰：「臣既小人，備荷驅使，緣百口在南，致拒皇略，罪合萬死。」

translations.literal: Boyu replied: "Your subject is a petty man, prepared to be driven; because a hundred mouths were in the south I resisted the imperial plan—crime fitting ten thousand deaths."
translations.idiomatic: Boyu said, "I am a petty man under orders; because my family remained in the south I resisted— deserving death ten thousand times."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「凡立忠抱節，皆應有所至。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "All who establish loyalty and hold to integrity should have something they reach toward.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Loyalty must have its proper object.

sentences.zh: 若奉逆君，守迷節，古人所不為。

translations.literal: To serve a rebellious lord and hold to a deluded integrity—men of antiquity did not do this.
translations.idiomatic: Serving a usurper while claiming integrity— the ancients did not do that.

sentences.zh: 卿何得事逆賊蕭鸞，自貽伊譴！」

translations.literal: How could you serve the rebellious minion Xiao Luan and bring this punishment on yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: How could you serve Xiao Luan and bring this on yourself?"

sentences.zh: 伯玉對曰：「臣愚癡晚悟，罪合萬斬，今遭陛下，願乞生命。」

translations.literal: Boyu replied: "Your subject is foolish and slow to understand; crime fitting ten thousand beheadings; now encountering Your Majesty I beg for life."
translations.idiomatic: Boyu said, "I was slow to understand and deserve death; now I beg Your Majesty for my life."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「凡人惟有兩途：知機獲褔，背機受禍。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Every man has only two paths: know the moment and obtain blessing, turn your back on the moment and receive calamity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Every man has two paths— seize the moment and live, or resist and perish.

sentences.zh: 勞我王師，彌歷歲月，如此為降，何人有罪！

translations.literal: You tired our royal army for years—who would be guilty in such a surrender!
translations.idiomatic: You exhausted our armies for years— who would call such a surrender innocent?

sentences.zh: 且朕前遣舍人公孫延景城西共卿語云：『天無二日，土無二王。』

translations.literal: Moreover I earlier sent Attendant Gongsun Yanjing west of the city to speak with you saying 'Heaven has no second sun, earth no second king.'
translations.idiomatic: I sent Gongsun Yanjing to tell you, 'Heaven has no second sun.'"

sentences.zh: 卿答云：『在此不在彼。』

translations.literal: You answered: 'It is here, not there.'
translations.idiomatic: You answered, 'The throne is here, not there.'"

sentences.zh: 天道攸遠，變化無方，卿寧知今日在此不在彼乎？」

translations.literal: Heaven's way is far; change has no fixed form—do you know that today it is here and not there?"
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's way is vast and changeable— do you know whether today it is here or there?"

sentences.zh: 伯玉乞命而已，更無所言。

translations.literal: Boyu begged for life and had nothing more to say.
translations.idiomatic: Boyu could only beg for life and said no more.

sentences.zh: 高祖以思安頻為伯玉泣請，故特宥之。

translations.literal: Because Si'an repeatedly wept and pleaded for Boyu, he was specially pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Because Si'an pleaded for him repeatedly, the emperor specially pardoned Boyu.

sentences.zh: 伯玉在南之日，放妾楊氏為尼。

translations.literal: When Boyu was in the south he released his concubine Lady Yang to become a nun.
translations.idiomatic: In the south Boyu had sent his concubine Lady Yang to become a nun.

sentences.zh: 入國，遂令還俗，復愛幸焉。

translations.literal: Entering the state he then ordered her to return to lay life and again favored her.
translations.idiomatic: In the north he had her return to lay life and favored her again.

sentences.zh: 為有司所奏，高祖聽之。

translations.literal: The authorities memorialized this and Emperor Gaozu permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities reported this and Emperor Gaozu allowed it.

sentences.zh: [10]世宗即位，拜長史，兼游擊將軍，出為馮翊相，卒官。

translations.literal: [10] When Emperor Shizong took the throne he was appointed Chief Clerk and concurrently General of Mobile Strikes, went out as Administrator of Fengyi, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: [10] Under Emperor Shizong he became chief clerk and General of Mobile Strikes, served as Administrator of Fengyi, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 崇吉，少驍勇，為沈文秀中兵參軍。

translations.literal: Chongji from youth was valiant and served Shen Wenxiu as army staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Chongji was bold from youth and served Shen Wenxiu as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 及太原戍守傅靈越率眾棄郡南赴子勛，文秀以崇吉督郡事。

translations.literal: When the Taiyuan garrison commander Fu Lingyue led the masses and abandoned the commandery south to join Zixun, Wenxiu made Chongji oversee the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiyuan's Fu Lingyue abandoned his post for Zixun, Wenxiu put Chongji in charge of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 既而背文秀，同於劉彧。

translations.literal: Later he turned against Wenxiu and joined Liu Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He later turned against Wenxiu and joined Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 母叔在歷城，為崔道固所拘繫，又將致刑於市以恐之，而崇吉卒無所顧。

translations.literal: His mother and uncle were in Licheng, detained by Cui Daogu, who also intended to execute them in the market to terrify him, yet Chongji in the end showed no concern.
translations.idiomatic: His mother and uncle were held in Licheng; Daogu threatened to execute them publicly, yet Chongji showed no wavering.

sentences.zh: 會道固歸彧，乃出其母。

translations.literal: When Daogu returned to Yu he released his mother.
translations.idiomatic: When Daogu submitted to Yu he released Chongji's mother.

sentences.zh: 彧以崇吉為龍驤將軍、并州刺史，領太原太守，戍升城。

translations.literal: Yu made Chongji General of the Dragon Cavalry and Inspector of Bing, holding Taiyuan as Administrator and garrisoning Shengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yu made Chongji General of the Dragon Cavalry and Inspector of Bing, holding Taiyuan and garrisoning Shengcheng.

sentences.zh: 崇吉以其從兄靈獻為長史，姨兄賈延年為司馬。

translations.literal: Chongji made his cousin Lingxian chief clerk and his aunt's son Jia Yannian Chief Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Chongji made his cousin Lingxian chief clerk and his cousin Jia Yannian chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 未幾而白曜軍至。

translations.literal: Before long Baiyao's army arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Baiyao's army arrived.

sentences.zh: 白曜遣人招之，崇吉不降，遂閉門固守。

translations.literal: Baiyao sent men to summon him; Chongji would not surrender and shut the gates to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao summoned him, but Chongji refused to yield and shut the gates.

sentences.zh: 升城至小，人力不多，勝仗者不過七百人，而白曜侮之，乃遣眾陵城。

translations.literal: Shengcheng was very small, manpower not great, and those with arms numbered no more than seven hundred; Baiyao despised it and sent troops to storm the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Shengcheng was tiny, with fewer than seven hundred armed men; Baiyao underestimated it and assaulted the walls.

sentences.zh: 崇吉設土蕇方梁，下相舂擊，不時克殄。

translations.literal: Chongji set earthen towers and crossbeams, striking from above and below, and could not quickly destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: Chongji raised earthworks and beams, beating back assaults, and the city held.

sentences.zh: 白曜遂築長城，圍三重，更造攻具，日夜攻擊。

translations.literal: Baiyao then built a long wall, encircling in three rings, and made new siege engines, attacking day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao built triple circumvallations and new siege engines, attacking day and night.

sentences.zh: 自二月至四月，糧矢俱盡，崇吉突圍出走，遁藏民舍，母妻見獲。

translations.literal: From the second month to the fourth, grain and arrows were exhausted; Chongji broke out and fled, hiding in a commoner's house; mother and wife were captured.
translations.idiomatic: From February to April supplies ran out; Chongji broke out, hid among the people, and his wife and mother were taken.

sentences.zh: 道固遣治中房靈賓慰引之，崇吉不肯見道固，遂東歸舊村，陰募壯士，欲以偷母，還奔河南。

translations.literal: Daogu sent Chief Clerk Fang Lingbin to comfort and summon him; Chongji would not see Daogu, then returned east to his old village, secretly recruiting stalwarts, intending to steal his mother back and flee south to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Daogu sent Fang Lingbin to negotiate; Chongji refused, returned to his village, secretly raised men to rescue his mother, and planned to flee south.

sentences.zh: 白曜慮其如此，守備嚴固。

translations.literal: Baiyao feared he would do this and kept strict guard.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao anticipated this and tightened the guard.

sentences.zh: 後與法壽取盤陽，俱降。

translations.literal: Later with Fashou he took Panyang and both surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined Fashou in taking Panyang and both submitted.

sentences.zh: 及立平齊郡，以歷城民為歸安縣，崇吉為縣令。

translations.literal: When Pingqi Commandery was established the people of Licheng were made Gui'an County and Chongji was made magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: When Pingqi was organized, Licheng became Gui'an County with Chongji as magistrate.

sentences.zh: 頗懷昔憾，與道固接事，意甚不平。

translations.literal: He harbored old resentment; dealing with Daogu he was very discontent.
translations.idiomatic: He nursed old grievances and was bitter when dealing with Daogu.

sentences.zh: 後委縣出臺，訟道固罪狀數條。

translations.literal: Later he left the county and went to the capital, accusing Daogu of several counts of crime.
translations.idiomatic: He later left his post and sued Daogu on several charges at court.

sentences.zh: 會赦不問。

translations.literal: An amnesty came and the matter was not pursued.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty intervened and the case was dropped.

sentences.zh: 崇吉乞解縣，許之。

translations.literal: Chongji begged to be relieved of the county post and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Chongji asked to resign the magistracy and was allowed.

sentences.zh: 停京師半歲，乃南奔。

translations.literal: He stayed in the capital half a year, then fled south.
translations.idiomatic: After half a year in the capital he fled south.

sentences.zh: 崇吉夫婦異路，剃髮為沙門，改名僧達，投其族叔法延。

translations.literal: Chongji and his wife took different routes, shaved their heads as monks, changed his name to Sengda, and went to his clansman Fayan.
translations.idiomatic: Husband and wife traveled separately, shaved their heads as monks, Chongji taking the name Sengda, and sought refuge with his kinsman Fayan.

sentences.zh: 住歲餘，清河張略之亦豪俠士也，崇吉遺其金帛，得以自遣。

translations.literal: After more than a year Zhang Lüezhi of Qinghe, also a bold knight, received Chongji's gold and silk and enabled his escape.
translations.idiomatic: After a year the Qinghe knight Zhang Lüezhi, aided by Chongji's gifts, helped him escape.

sentences.zh: 妻從幽州南出，亦得相會。

translations.literal: His wife went south from Youzhou and they were able to meet.
translations.idiomatic: His wife came south from Youzhou and they reunited.

sentences.zh: 崇吉至江東，尋病死。

translations.literal: Chongji reached the eastern bank of the Yangzi and soon died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Chongji reached the south and soon died.

sentences.zh: 崇吉從父弟三益，字敬安，於南陽內附。

translations.literal: Chongji's cousin Sanyi, courtesy name Jing'an, submitted from Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chongji's cousin Sanyi, courtesy name Jing'an, submitted from Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖與語，善之，曰：「三益了了，殊不惡。」

translations.literal: The emperor spoke with him, liked him, and said: "Sanyi is clear-minded—by no means bad."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor met him, was pleased, and said, "Sanyi is sharp—quite promising."

sentences.zh: 拜員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Outer Palace Cavalier Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Outer Palace Cavalier Attendant.

sentences.zh: 尋出為太山太守，轉兗州左軍府司馬，所在以清和著稱。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as Administrator of Taishan, then Chief Commandant in the Left Army of Yanzhou; wherever he served he was famed for clarity and harmony.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Administrator of Taishan and then on Yanzhou's left army staff, earning repute for fair and humane rule.

sentences.zh: 還，除左將軍。

translations.literal: On return he was made General of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was made General of the Left.

sentences.zh: 正光中卒，年六十三。

translations.literal: He died in the Zhengguang era at age sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died during Zhengguang at sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 九子。

translations.literal: Nine sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had nine sons.

sentences.zh: 長子士隆，興和中，東清河太守，帶盤陽鎮將。

translations.literal: The eldest son Shilong in the Xinghe era was Administrator of Eastern Qinghe and concurrently garrison commander of Panyang.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest, Shilong, during Xinghe governed Eastern Qinghe and commanded the Panyang garrison.

sentences.zh: 士隆弟士達，少有才氣。

translations.literal: Shilong's younger brother Shida from youth had talent and spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong's brother Shida was talented and spirited from youth.

sentences.zh: 其族兄景先，有鑒識，每曰：「此兒俶儻，終當大其門戶。」

translations.literal: His clansman Jingxian had discernment and often said: "This boy is bold and will eventually enlarge his house."
translations.idiomatic: His kinsman Jingxian often said, "This lad is daring and will glorify the clan."

sentences.zh: 起家濟州左將軍府倉曹參軍。

translations.literal: He began his career as Granary Officer in the Left General's office of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He began as granary officer on Ji Province's left army staff.

sentences.zh: 時京兆王繼為大將軍，出鎮關右，聞其名，徵補騎兵參軍，領帳內統軍。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Ji of Jingzhao was Grand General and went out to garrison the west of the pass; hearing his name he summoned and appointed him Cavalry Commandant in charge of the inner guard corps.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ji of Jingzhao, campaigning west, heard of him and made him cavalry commandant of his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，其鄉人劉蒼生、劉鈞、房須等作亂，攻陷郡縣，頻敗州軍。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era his townsman Liu Cangsheng, Liu Jun, Fang Xu, and others rebelled, took commanderies and counties, and repeatedly defeated provincial troops.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiaochang, local leaders Liu Cangsheng, Liu Jun, and Fang Xu rebelled, seized districts, and repeatedly beat provincial troops.

sentences.zh: 時士達父憂在家，刺史元欣欲逼其為將，士達以禮固辭。

translations.literal: At that time Shida was at home in mourning for his father; Inspector Yuan Xin wished to force him to be general, but Shida firmly declined on grounds of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Shida was mourning his father when Inspector Yuan Xin tried to force him into command; he refused on ritual grounds.

sentences.zh: 欣乃命其友人馮元興謂之曰：「今合境從逆，賊徒轉熾，若萬一陷州，君家豈得獨全？

translations.literal: Xin then ordered his friend Feng Yuanxing to tell him: "Now the whole region follows the rebels and bandits grow fiercer; if the province should fall, could your family alone remain whole?
translations.idiomatic: Xin had Feng Yuanxing urge him, "The whole region rebels—if the province falls, can your family survive alone?

sentences.zh: 既急病如此，安得顧名教也。」

translations.literal: With urgent illness such as this, how can one heed name and teaching!"
translations.idiomatic: In such a crisis, how can you cling to propriety?"

sentences.zh: 士達不得已而起，率州郭之人二千餘人，東西討擊，悉破平之。

translations.literal: Shida had no choice but to rise, leading more than two thousand people of the provincial city east and west in punitive attack, and completely defeated and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Shida reluctantly rallied over two thousand men, crushed the rebels in every direction, and restored order.

sentences.zh: 武泰初，就家拜平原太守，抑挫豪強，境內肅然。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wutai he was appointed Administrator of Pingyuan at home, suppressed the powerful, and the territory was orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wutai he became Administrator of Pingyuan, curbed the powerful, and restored order.

sentences.zh: 時邢杲寇亂，憚其威名，越郡城西度，不敢攻逼。

translations.literal: At that time Xing Gao raided in disorder; he feared Shida's martial name and crossed west of the commandery, not daring to press the attack.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Xing Gao feared his reputation and marched west of the commandery without attacking.

sentences.zh: 永安末，轉濟南太守。

translations.literal: At the end of Yong'an he was transferred Administrator of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Yong'an he was transferred to Jinan.

sentences.zh: 士達不入京師，而頻為本州郡，時人榮之。

translations.literal: Shida did not enter the capital but frequently served his home province and commandery; men of the time honored this.
translations.idiomatic: Shida never went to the capital but repeatedly served his home region—a point of honor.

sentences.zh: 永安末，尒朱兆入洛，刺史蕭贊為城民趙洛周所逐，城內無主。

translations.literal: At the end of Yong'an Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang; Inspector Xiao Zan was driven out by the city people Zhao Luozhou and the city had no lord.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Yong'an Erzhu Zhao seized Luoyang; Inspector Xiao Zan was expelled and the city was leaderless.

sentences.zh: 洛周等以士達鄉情所歸，乃就郡請之，命攝州事。

translations.literal: Luozhou and others because Shida was where township feeling returned asked him at the commandery and ordered him to act as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Luozhou and others, trusting local loyalty to Shida, asked him to govern the province.

sentences.zh: 永熙二年卒，年三十八，時人傷惜之。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Yongxi at age thirty-eight; men of the time mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Yongxi at thirty-eight, to general regret.

sentences.zh: 贈平東將軍、齊州刺史，諡曰武。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Qi with posthumous title Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Qi with the posthumous name Wu.

sentences.zh: 士達弟士素，武定末，太尉諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Shida's younger brother Shisu at the end of Wuding was Consultant in the Grand Marshal's office.
translations.idiomatic: Shida's brother Shisu ended as consultant in the Grand Marshal's office under Wuding.

sentences.zh: 士素弟士章，尚書郎。

translations.literal: Shisu's younger brother Shizhang was a Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Shisu's brother Shizhang was a gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 法壽族子景伯，字長暉。

translations.literal: Fashou's clansman Jingbo, courtesy name Changhui.
translations.idiomatic: Fashou's kinsman Jingbo, courtesy name Changhui.

sentences.zh: 高祖諶，避地渡河，居於齊州之東清河繹幕焉。

translations.literal: High ancestor Chen crossed the river to escape trouble and settled in Yimo of Eastern Qinghe in Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: The clan ancestor Chen fled across the river and settled at Yimo in Eastern Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 祖元慶，仕劉駿，歷七郡太守，後為沈文秀青州建威府司馬。

translations.literal: Grandfather Yuanqing served Liu Jun, successively held seven commandery governorships, and later was Chief Commandant in Shen Wenxiu's Qingzhou Jianwei headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Yuanqing served Liu Jun as administrator of seven commanderies and later on Shen Wenxiu's Qingzhou staff.

sentences.zh: 劉彧之殺子業自立也，子業弟子勛起兵攻之，文秀遣其將劉珍之率兵助彧。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu killed Ziye and established himself, Ziye's nephew Zixun raised troops to attack him; Wenxiu sent his general Liu Zhenzhi with troops to aid Yu.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu killed Ziye and seized power, Zixun rebelled; Wenxiu sent Liu Zhenzhi to aid Yu.

sentences.zh: 後背彧歸于子勛，元慶不同，為文秀所害。

translations.literal: Later he turned against Yu and returned to Zixun; Yuanqing did not agree and was killed by Wenxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu later defected to Zixun; Yuanqing refused and was killed.

sentences.zh: 父愛親，率勒鄉部攻文秀。

translations.literal: Father Aiqin led the township to attack Wenxiu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Aiqin led the township against Wenxiu.

sentences.zh: 劉彧嘉之，起家授龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: Liu Yu commended this and at first appointment made him General of the Dragon Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu praised him and first made him General of the Dragon Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 尋會文秀降彧，乃止。

translations.literal: Soon Wenxiu surrendered to Yu and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxiu submitted to Yu, he stood down.

sentences.zh: 顯祖時，三齊平，隨例內徙，為平齊民。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xianzu's time the three Qi were pacified and by precedent they moved inward, becoming Pingqi people.
translations.idiomatic: When the three Qi fell under Emperor Xianzu, the family was resettled as Pingqi subjects.

sentences.zh: 以父非命，疏服終身。

translations.literal: Because his father died by violence he wore coarse garments all his life.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's violent death he wore mourning garb for life.

sentences.zh: 景伯生於桑乾，少喪父，以孝聞。

translations.literal: Jingbo was born at Sanggan; he lost his father young and was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Jingbo was born at Sanggan, lost his father young, and was famed for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 家貧，傭書自給，養母甚謹。

translations.literal: The family was poor; he copied books to support himself and nourished his mother with great care.
translations.idiomatic: Poor, he copied books for a living and cared for his mother devotedly.

sentences.zh: 尚書盧淵稱之於李沖，沖時典選，拔為奉朝請、司空祭酒、給事中、尚書儀曹郎。

translations.literal: Minister Lu Yuan praised him to Li Chong; Chong then held selection and promoted him Gentleman at Court, Libationer of the Minister of Works, Attendant, and Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yuan recommended him to Li Chong, who appointed him court gentleman, libationer, attendant, and ritual officer.

sentences.zh: 除齊州輔國長史，值刺史死，敕行州事。

translations.literal: He was made Chief Clerk who Supports the State in Qi Province; when the inspector died an edict ordered him to act in provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He became chief clerk in Qi; when the inspector died he was ordered to govern the province.

sentences.zh: 政存寬簡，百姓安之。

translations.literal: His government was lenient and simple and the people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was lenient and the people were at peace.

sentences.zh: 後值清河太守杜昶外叛，郡居山險，盜賊羣起，除清河太守。

translations.literal: Later when Administrator of Qinghe Du Chang rebelled abroad, the commandery lay in mountain peril and bandits rose in groups; he was made Administrator of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: When Qinghe's Du Chang rebelled and bandits swarmed the hills, he was made administrator.

sentences.zh: 郡民劉簡虎曾失禮於景伯，聞其臨郡，闔家逃亡。

translations.literal: The commandery man Liu Jianhu had once been rude to Jingbo; hearing he was coming to the commandery, the whole family fled.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jianhu, who had once insulted him, fled with his whole family when Jingbo arrived.

sentences.zh: 景伯督切屬縣捕擒之，即署其子為西曹掾，命喻山賊。

translations.literal: Jingbo urged the subordinate counties to seize him, then appointed his son Western Clerk and ordered him to persuade the mountain bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Jingbo had him captured, appointed his son clerk, and sent him to persuade the mountain bandits.

sentences.zh: 賊以景伯不念舊惡，一時俱下，論者稱之。

translations.literal: The bandits, because Jingbo did not bear old wrongs, all came down at once; discussants praised this.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits, seeing he bore no grudge, surrendered en masse—to general praise.

sentences.zh: 舊守令六年為限，限滿將代，郡民韓靈和等三百餘人表訴乞留，復加二載。

translations.literal: Formerly prefects and magistrates had a six-year term; when the term was full and replacement was due, more than three hundred commandery people including Han Linghe memorialized begging to retain him, and two more years were added.
translations.idiomatic: When his six-year term ended, three hundred locals petitioned to keep him, and he served two more years.

sentences.zh: 後遷太尉中郎、司徒諮議參軍、輔國將軍、司空長史。

translations.literal: Later he was moved Grand Master in the Grand Marshal's office, Consultant in the Secretariat, General Who Supports the State, and Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He later served in the Grand Marshal's and Secretariat offices and as the Minister of Works' chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 以母疾去官。

translations.literal: He left office because of his mother's illness.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned when his mother fell ill.

sentences.zh: 景伯性淳和，涉獵經史，諸弟宗之，如事嚴親。

translations.literal: Jingbo was by nature pure and harmonious, dipped into the classics and histories, and the younger brothers revered him as if to a stern parent.
translations.idiomatic: Jingbo was gentle, widely read, and his brothers revered him like a father.

sentences.zh: 及弟妓亡，[11]蔬食終喪，期不內御，憂毀之容，有如居重。

translations.literal: When a younger brother's concubine died, [11] he ate vegetables through the mourning period, for a year took no wife within, and his grieving appearance was as if in heavy mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When a younger brother's concubine died, [11] he ate plain food through mourning, abstained from the inner chambers for a year, and grieved as for a parent.

sentences.zh: 其次弟景先亡，其幼弟景遠期年哭臨，亦不內寢。

translations.literal: When his next younger brother Jingxian died, his youngest brother Jingyuan for a year wailed at the bier and also did not sleep within.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingxian died, the youngest brother Jingyuan mourned a full year without entering the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 鄉里為之語曰：「有義有禮，房家兄弟。」

translations.literal: The township made a saying: "With righteousness and ritual—the Fang brothers."
translations.idiomatic: Locals said, "Righteous and ritual-minded—the Fang brothers."

sentences.zh: 廷尉卿崔光韶好標牓人物，[12]無所推尚，每云景伯有士大夫之行業。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Cui Guangshao loved to label men of character, [12] recommending none lightly; he always said Jingbo had the conduct and achievement of a grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Cui Guangshao, [12] who rarely praised anyone, said Jingbo had a true gentleman's conduct.

sentences.zh: 及母亡，景伯居喪，不食鹽菜，因此遂為水病，積年不愈。

translations.literal: When his mother died Jingbo mourned, ate no salt or vegetables, and therefore developed water illness, uncured for many years.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning his mother, he ate no salt or vegetables, fell ill with edema, and never fully recovered.

sentences.zh: 孝昌三年卒于家，時年五十。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiaochang he died at home at age fifty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home in the third year of Xiaochang at fifty.

sentences.zh: 贈左將軍、齊州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made General of the Left and Inspector of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General of the Left and Inspector of Qi.

sentences.zh: 子文烈，武定中，尚書三公郎中。

translations.literal: His son Wenlie in the Wuding era was Gentleman in the Three Dukes Bureau of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wenlie under Wuding served in the Three Dukes Bureau.

sentences.zh: 景先，字光冑。

translations.literal: Jingxian, courtesy name Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian, whose courtesy name was Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 幼孤貧，無資從師，其母自授毛詩、曲禮。

translations.literal: Orphaned young and poor, without means to follow a teacher, his mother herself taught him the Mao Odes and the Record of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor, he could not afford a teacher; his mother taught him the Mao Odes and the Record of Rites.

sentences.zh: 年十二，請其母曰：「豈可使兄傭賃以供景先也？

translations.literal: At age twelve he asked his mother: "How can I let my elder brother hire himself out to supply Jingxian?
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he told his mother, "I cannot let my brother hire himself out to pay for my schooling.

sentences.zh: 請自求衣，然後就學。」

translations.literal: I beg to seek my own clothes and then go to study."
translations.idiomatic: Let me earn my own clothes, then study."

sentences.zh: 母哀其小，不許。

translations.literal: The mother pitied his youth and did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, pitying his youth, refused.

sentences.zh: 苦請，從之，遂得一羊裘，忻然自足。

translations.literal: He begged bitterly; she complied, and he obtained one sheepskin coat and was happily content.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded until she agreed; he got a sheepskin coat and was content.

sentences.zh: 晝則樵蘇，夜誦經史，自是精勤，遂大通贍。

translations.literal: By day he gathered firewood; by night he recited the classics and histories; from this he became diligent and thoroughly mastered them.
translations.idiomatic: By day he gathered fuel; by night he read the classics until he mastered them.

sentences.zh: 太和中，例得還鄉，郡辟功曹。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era by precedent he was able to return home; the commandery recruited him as Merit Officer.
translations.idiomatic: During Taihe he returned home and was recruited as merit officer.

sentences.zh: 州舉秀才，值州將卒，不得對策。

translations.literal: The province nominated him as Presented Scholar; the provincial commander died and he could not answer at examination.
translations.idiomatic: The province nominated him presented scholar, but the commander died before he could sit the examination.

sentences.zh: 解褐太學博士。

translations.literal: He left the sackcloth and was made Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 時太常劉芳、侍中崔光當世儒宗，歎其精博，光遂奏兼著作佐郎，修國史。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Master of Ceremonies Liu Fang and Attendant Cui Guang were the age's Confucian leaders; they sighed at his mastery; Guang then memorialized him as concurrent Editorial Assistant, revising the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang and Cui Guang, leading scholars of the age, admired his learning; Guang had him appointed editorial assistant on the national history.

sentences.zh: 尋除司徒祭酒、員外郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Libationer of the Secretariat and Outer Palace Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became libationer of the Secretariat and outer palace gentleman.

sentences.zh: 侍中穆紹又啟景先撰世宗起居注。

translations.literal: Attendant Mu Shao also memorialized Jingxian to compile Emperor Shizong's Diaries of Activity and Repose.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Mu Shao also had him compile Emperor Shizong's court diary.

sentences.zh: 累遷步兵校尉，領尚書郎，齊州中正，所歷皆有當官之稱。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted Colonel Director of Footsoldiers, leading Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, and Chief Rectifier of Qi Province; in every post he had the reputation of fitting the office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through military and secretariat posts and as chief rectifier of Qi, excelling in every office.

sentences.zh: 景先沉敏方正，事兄恭謹，出告反面，晨昏參省，側立移時，兄亦危坐，相敬如對賓客。

translations.literal: Jingxian was deep, keen, and upright; serving his elder brother with reverent care, going out and returning he reported; morning and evening he attended; standing to the side for long intervals, the elder brother also sat upright—they respected each other as if facing guests.
translations.idiomatic: Deep, sharp, and upright, he served his brother with ritual punctilio—they treated each other like honored guests.

sentences.zh: 兄曾寢疾，景先侍湯藥，衣冠不解，形容毀瘁。

translations.literal: When his elder brother once lay ill Jingxian attended medicines, did not remove cap or belt, and his appearance was wasted.
translations.idiomatic: When his brother fell ill he nursed him without undressing, haggard with care.

sentences.zh: 親友見者莫不哀之。

translations.literal: Kin and friends who saw it were all grieved.
translations.idiomatic: Kin and friends were moved to grief.

sentences.zh: 神龜元年，蕭衍龍驤將軍田申能據東義陽城內屬，敕景先為行臺，發二荊兵以援之，在軍遇疾而還。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shengui Xiao Yan's General of the Dragon Cavalry Tian Shenneng held Dongyiyang city and submitted inward; an edict ordered Jingxian as mobile staff, sending the two Jing armies to aid; in the army he fell ill and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengui, when a Liang general held Dongyiyang and submitted, Jingxian was sent with Jing troops to aid; he fell ill and returned.

sentences.zh: 其年卒於家，時年四十三。

translations.literal: That year he died at home at age forty-three.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died at home at forty-three.

sentences.zh: 贈持節、冠軍將軍、洛州刺史，諡曰文景。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the staff, General of the Champions, and Inspector of Luo with posthumous title Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given the staff, made General of the Champions and Inspector of Luo, with the posthumous name Wenjing.

sentences.zh: 先作五經疑問百餘篇，其言該典，今行於時，文多，略舉其切於世教者：

translations.literal: He first composed more than a hundred chapters of Doubts on the Five Classics; his words are comprehensive and canonical and circulate in the age; the text is long—here a summary of what bears on worldly teaching:
translations.idiomatic: He had earlier written more than a hundred chapters of Doubts on the Five Classics; though the full text is extensive, what follows samples passages relevant to moral teaching:

sentences.zh: 問王者受命，木火相生曰：五精代感，禀靈者興。

translations.literal: Question: When the king receives the mandate, wood and fire mutually generate—says: The five essences succeed in sensation; those who receive the numinous rise.
translations.idiomatic: Question on the king's receiving the mandate and the mutual generation of wood and fire: The five agents succeed one another in turn, and those who receive the numinous ascend.

sentences.zh: 金德方隆，禎發華渚；

translations.literal: The metal virtue flourished grandly and auspiciousness arose at Hua Zhu;
translations.idiomatic: When the metal phase rose in glory, auspicious signs appeared at Hua Zhu;

sentences.zh: 水運告昌，瑤光啟祚。

translations.literal: the water fortune announced prosperity and Yaoguang began the throne.
translations.idiomatic: when the water phase proclaimed prosperity, Yaoguang inaugurated the reign.

sentences.zh: 人道承天，天理應實，受謝既彰，玄命若契。

translations.literal: The human way follows heaven; heaven's principle responds to reality; receiving the abdication is already manifest, the dark mandate like a covenant.
translations.idiomatic: Human order follows heaven; heaven's principle answers to reality; the transfer of mandate is manifest, the hidden decree like a bond.

sentences.zh: 相生之義，有允不違。

translations.literal: The meaning of mutual generation has allowance and does not violate.
translations.idiomatic: Mutual generation is consistent and not contradictory.

sentences.zh: 至如湯武革命，殺伐是用，水火為次，遵而不改。

translations.literal: As for Tang and Wu's revolution, killing and attack were used; water and fire came next, followed without change.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Tang and Wu revolutionized, they used force; water followed fire in the sequence without alteration.

sentences.zh: 既事乖代終，而數同納麓。

translations.literal: Since the affair opposed the end of a dynasty yet the numbers matched receiving the map at the foot of the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Though their acts ended a dynasty, their numbers still matched receiving the mandate.

sentences.zh: 逆順且殊，禎運宜異，而兆徵不差，有疑符應。

translations.literal: Rebellion and submission differ, yet auspicious fortune should differ; yet omens were not wrong—there is doubt about the correspondence of signs.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion and submission differ, yet omens did not diverge—is the sign-system therefore doubtful?

sentences.zh: 問禹以鯀配天，舜不尊父曰：明明上天，下土是冒。

translations.literal: Question: Yu made Gun match heaven; Shun did not honor his father—says: Bright bright above heaven, below earth is covered.
translations.idiomatic: Question: Yu paired Gun with Heaven though Shun did not honor his father—'Bright is Heaven above, covering earth below.'

sentences.zh: 道高者負扆四方，神積者郊原斯主。

translations.literal: The way is high for those who bear the screen on four sides; spirit accumulates for those who are lord of the suburbs and plains.
translations.idiomatic: The highest way burdens the ruler who faces four directions; accumulated spirit makes one lord of field and altar.

sentences.zh: 是以則天，不能私其子；

translations.literal: Therefore regulating heaven cannot privately favor one's son;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore regulating heaven cannot favor one's son privately;

sentences.zh: 紹堯，不敢尊其父。

translations.literal: succeeding Yao cannot boldly honor one's father.
translations.idiomatic: succeeding Yao cannot boldly exalt one's father.

sentences.zh: 鯀既罪彰於山川，受殛於羽裔，化質與鱗甲為群。

translations.literal: Gun's crime was manifest in mountains and rivers, receiving execution in the feathered outskirts; his transformed substance joined scales and shells in a crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Gun's guilt was shown in mountains and rivers; he was executed in the wilds and became a creature among fish and reptiles.

sentences.zh: 銘精不能上乘箕尾，而厚尊配於國陽，當升煙之大禮。

translations.literal: His refined spirit could not ascend to the Tail and Winnowing Basket, yet he was greatly honored and paired at Guoyang in the great smoke-offering rite.
translations.idiomatic: His spirit could not ascend to the stars, yet he was grandly honored at Guoyang in the great sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 苟存及躬，以亂祀典。

translations.literal: If one preserves benefit to the person and thereby disorders the sacrificial canon.
translations.idiomatic: If one preserves personal benefit and thereby disorders the sacrificial canon—

sentences.zh: 降上帝為罪鬼之賓，奏夾鍾為介蟲之樂，奉天之道，不乃有淪乎？

translations.literal: Lowering the Lord on High to be guest of guilty ghosts, playing the jiazhong for music of creeping things—serving heaven's way, is it not fallen?
translations.idiomatic: making the Lord on High guest to guilty ghosts and playing the jiazhong for creeping things—has not the way of serving heaven collapsed?

sentences.zh: 問湯尊稷廢柱曰：神積道存，異世同尊；

translations.literal: Question: Tang honored Ji and demoted Zhu—says: Spirit accumulates and the way endures; different ages share the same honor;
translations.idiomatic: Question: Tang honored Ji and demoted Zhu—'Spirit endures and the way abides; different ages honor alike;'

sentences.zh: 列山見享，綿紀前代。

translations.literal: Lie Mountain was seen in sacrifice, continuing through former ages.
translations.idiomatic: Lie Mountain was sacrificed to through former ages.

sentences.zh: 成湯革命承天，當愆陽之運，不思理數之有時，黜元功於百世。

translations.literal: Cheng Tang's revolution received heaven; when it should have been the yang's turn in fate, he did not think of the seasons of principle and number, and demoted the primal merit for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Tang received heaven's mandate yet, in a yang period of fate, demoted primal merit for a hundred generations without regard to cosmic timing.

sentences.zh: 且畢、箕感應，風雨異徵，尊播殖之靈，而邀滂澍之潤，升廢之道，無乃謬與？

translations.literal: Moreover Bi and Ji responded to feeling; wind and rain had different signs; honoring the spirit of sowing yet seeking the favor of pouring rain—elevating what was demoted, is it not absurd?
translations.idiomatic: Bi and Ji answered with wind and rain in differing signs—honoring the grain spirit while begging rain— is not elevating the demoted absurd?

sentences.zh: 若柱不合薦，虞夏應失之於前；

translations.literal: If Zhu were unfit for recommendation, Yu and Xia should have lost it before;
translations.idiomatic: If Zhu were unworthy of sacrifice, Yu and Xia should have erred earlier;

sentences.zh: 如以歲久宜遷，百神可計日而代。

translations.literal: if because long years should shift, the hundred spirits could be replaced day by day.
translations.idiomatic: if because time passes one should shift altars, the hundred spirits could be replaced daily.

sentences.zh: 求之二三，未究往旨。

translations.literal: Seeking it in two or three places, the former intent is not yet investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing this in several texts, the ancients' intent is still unclear.

sentences.zh: 問湯克桀，欲遷夏社為不可；

translations.literal: Question: Tang overcame Jie and wished to move the Xia altar—this could not be done;
translations.idiomatic: Question: Tang overcame Jie and wished to move the Xia altar but could not;

sentences.zh: 武王滅紂，以亳社為亡國之誡曰：神無定方，唯人為主，道協無為，天地是依，棄德弗崇，百靈更祀。

translations.literal: Wu Wang destroyed Zhou and took the Bo altar as the warning of a perished state—says: Spirits have no fixed place; only man is lord; the way joins non-action; heaven and earth are relied upon; abandoning virtue and not honoring, the hundred spirits change sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu destroyed Zhou and used the Bo altar as warning of a fallen state—'Spirits have no fixed place; only man is lord; abandon virtue and the hundred spirits change their worship.'

sentences.zh: 周武承天，禮存咸秩，升后稷當四圭之尊，貶土祇隔牲幣之享。

translations.literal: Zhou Wu received heaven; ritual preserved the full order; elevating Hou Ji to the honor of four jade scepters, demoting the earth lord to separate victim and silk offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wu received heaven, yet elevated Hou Ji to four-jade honor while demoting the earth lord to lesser offerings.

sentences.zh: 就如言之，稷禀靈威，誠允聿追之宜，社非商祖，孝孚乃考之咎，殷鑒致誡，何獨在斯？

translations.literal: If as the words say, Ji received numinous majesty and truly should be pursued in elevation, the earth lord was not Shang's ancestor—filial trust is the father's fault; why is Yin alone given warning here?
translations.idiomatic: If Ji truly deserved elevation, the earth lord was not Shang's ancestor—why is only Yin singled out for warning?

sentences.zh: 問易著革命之爻，而無揖讓之象曰：玄黃剖別，人道為尊，含靈佇化，故義始元首。

translations.literal: Question: The Changes sets forth the hexagram of revolution yet has no image of yielding—says: Black and yellow were split apart and the human way became honored; containing spirit awaiting transformation, therefore righteousness begins at the head.
translations.idiomatic: Question: The Changes presents revolution yet no yielding—'When heaven and earth divided, the human way was honored and rule began with the sovereign.'

sentences.zh: 是以飛龍啟徵，大人載就。

translations.literal: Therefore the flying dragon opens the omen and the great man is established.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the flying dragon opens the sign and the great man is established.

sentences.zh: 及理運相推，帝圖異序。

translations.literal: When principle's fortune pushes one another, imperial diagrams differ in order.
translations.idiomatic: When dynastic fortune shifts, imperial orders differ in sequence.

sentences.zh: 虞賓以為善終順守，有慚未盡，不顯揖讓之象，而著已日之美。

translations.literal: Shun as guest was a good end and obedient keeping, yet had the shame of not fully exhausting; not displaying the image of yielding, yet showing the beauty of 'already day'—
translations.idiomatic: Shun's yielding as guest was a fine ending, yet incomplete; the Changes shows 'already day' without displaying full yielding—

sentences.zh: 豈可兆巨釁為貽厥之謀，訓萬世而開安忍之□？

translations.literal: how can one take great treason as a plan to bequeath to posterity, instruct ten thousand generations and open the gate of cruel forbearance [damaged character]?
translations.idiomatic: how can great treason bequeath a plan to posterity and teach ten thousand generations cruel forbearance [text damaged]?

sentences.zh: 求之反衷，未識理恕。

translations.literal: Seeking the contrary in the inner, one does not yet know principle's forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Judged by inner principle, this is hard to reconcile with forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 問周禮秋官司烜氏，邦若屋誅，為明竁焉曰：王道貴產，法理尚恩。

translations.literal: Question: The Rites of Zhou, Autumn Office, Torch Master—if the state executes house punishment, make a bright tomb—says: The kingly way values life; legal principle honors grace.
translations.idiomatic: Question: In the Rites of Zhou the Torch Master, when the state executes house punishment, makes a bright tomb—'The kingly way values life; law honors grace.'

sentences.zh: 舊德見食，八象載其美；

translations.literal: Old virtue is fed; the eight signs bear their beauty;
translations.idiomatic: Old merit is nourished; the eight signs bear their beauty;

sentences.zh: 五宥三刺，禮經寶其仁。

translations.literal: the five pardons and three interrogations—ritual classics treasure their humanity.
translations.idiomatic: the five pardons and three interrogations—the classics treasure humanity.

sentences.zh: 是以祿父巨釁，殷禮不輟；

translations.literal: Therefore the father of Lu's enfeoffment had great fault yet Yin ritual was not stopped;
translations.idiomatic: thus Lu's enfeoffed father had great fault yet Yin rites continued;

sentences.zh: 三監亂德，蔡胤猶存。

translations.literal: the Three Overseers disordered virtue yet Cai Yin still survived.
translations.idiomatic: the Three Overseers rebelled yet Cai Yin still survived.

sentences.zh: 罪莫極於無上，逆莫甚於違天。

translations.literal: Crime has nothing beyond lacking a superior; rebellion has nothing worse than violating heaven.
translations.idiomatic: No crime exceeds treason against heaven.

sentences.zh: 行大辟禍不及族，理正刑愆止於身。

translations.literal: Executing the great punishment—calamity does not reach the clan; principle corrects punishment and guilt stops at the person.
translations.idiomatic: In capital punishment calamity should not reach the clan; guilt should stop with the person.

sentences.zh: 何惡當參夷之禍？

translations.literal: What evil deserves the calamity of exterminating the kindred?
translations.idiomatic: What evil deserves extermination of the clan?

sentences.zh: 何戾受淪殄之辜？

translations.literal: What offense receives the guilt of total destruction?
translations.idiomatic: What offense deserves total destruction?

sentences.zh: 問儀禮，繼母出嫁，從為之服，傳云「貴終其恩」曰：繼母配父，本非天屬，與尊合德，名義以興。

translations.literal: Question: In the Ritual, when the stepmother marries out, one follows her in mourning; the commentary says 'honor the end of her kindness'—says: The stepmother matches the father; originally not heaven's kin; with honor united in virtue, name and righteousness arise.
translations.idiomatic: Question: When a stepmother remarries, the Ritual says one follows her in mourning because one 'honors the end of her kindness'—a stepmother is not kin by nature but gains standing through the father.

sentences.zh: 兼鞠育有加，禮服是重。

translations.literal: Moreover rearing and nurturing add to it; ritual garments are weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Raising and nurturing add obligation; ritual garments are weighty.

sentences.zh: 既體違義盡，棄節毀慈，作嬪異門，為鬼他族，神道不全，何終恩之有？

translations.literal: Once the body violates righteousness to the end, abandons integrity and destroys kindness, becomes consort in another gate and ghost of another clan—spirit's way incomplete, how is there 'end of kindness'?
translations.idiomatic: If she destroys kindness, joins another house, and becomes ghost of another clan—how can kindness be 'ended' in mourning?

sentences.zh: 方齊服是追，哭於野次，苟存降重，無乃過猶不及乎？

translations.literal: To pursue qi garments in mourning and weep in the wild—if merely preserving lowered weight, is it not excess rather than deficiency?
translations.idiomatic: To wear qi mourning and weep in the wild—is that not going beyond what is due?

sentences.zh: 問禮記，生不及祖父母，父母稅喪，己則否曰：服以恩制，禮由義立。

translations.literal: Question: In the Record of Rites, if one is born too late to know grandparents, parents wear tax mourning but oneself does not—says: Garments follow kindness; ritual stands on righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Question: The Record of Rites says if one never knew grandparents, parents wear tax mourning but the grandchild does not—'Garments follow affection; ritual stands on righteousness.'

sentences.zh: 慈母三年，孫無緦葛者，以戚非天屬，報養止身。

translations.literal: The loving mother three years; the grandson has no hemp garment—because the sorrow is not heaven's kin, repaying nurture stops at the person.
translations.idiomatic: A loving mother may be mourned three years, yet a grandson wears no hemp for grandparents he never knew—nurture, not blood, sets the limit.

sentences.zh: 祖雖異域，恩不及己，但正體於下，可無服乎？

translations.literal: Though the grandfather is in another region, kindness does not reach oneself—but as the correct body below, can there be no garment?
translations.idiomatic: Though grandparents are distant and kindness did not reach you, as their direct descendant can there be no mourning?

sentences.zh: 且縞冠玄武，子姓之服。

translations.literal: Moreover the white cap and dark robe are garments of the patriline.
translations.idiomatic: The white cap and dark robe are patrilineal mourning garb.

sentences.zh: 縓練之後，纕絰已除，猶懷慘素，未忍從吉，況斬焉。

translations.literal: After bleached and dyed cloth, the hemp sash is already removed; still cherishing somber plainness, not yet bearing to follow auspicious rites—how much more in the case of the hem.
translations.idiomatic: After the bleached and dyed stages the hemp is removed, yet one still wears somber garb and cannot yet accept joy—how much more in the case of the hem.

sentences.zh: 初之創巨方始，[13]復弔之賓，尚改緇襲，奉哀苫次，而無追變，孝子孝孫，豈天理是與？

translations.literal: At the first founding the great wound just begins, [13] guests coming to condole still change black for mourning dress and observe the bitter hut without pursuing change—filial son and filial grandson, is this not heaven's principle?
translations.idiomatic: When the great wound is fresh, [13] even condolence guests change to black—can filial sons ignore the change of garments required by principle?

sentences.zh: 問左氏傳，齊人殺哀姜，君子以為不可曰：受醮從天，人倫所重。

translations.literal: Question: In the Zuo Commentary, the Qi people killed Ai Jiang—the gentleman thought it impossible—says: Receiving the ritual cup from heaven, human relations are weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Question: The Zuo Commentary says the Qi killed Ai Jiang and the gentleman disapproved—'Receiving the ritual cup from heaven, human relations are weighty.'

sentences.zh: 保育異宗，承奉郊奠。

translations.literal: Nurturing in another clan, undertaking the suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: She was nurtured in another clan and undertook the suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 而乃肆極昏淫，禍傾合卺之尊；

translations.literal: Yet she wildly practiced extreme debauchery, calamity overturning the honor of the marriage rite;
translations.idiomatic: Yet she practiced extreme debauchery, overturning the honor of marriage;

sentences.zh: 怙亂無終，殄滅誕鞠之愛。

translations.literal: relying on disorder without end, extinguishing the love of the child she bore.
translations.idiomatic: relying on disorder without end, destroying love for the child she bore.

sentences.zh: 齊桓匡翼四方，正存刑矩。

translations.literal: Duke Huan of Qi rectified and aided the four quarters, preserving punishment as measure.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan of Qi rectified the four quarters and preserved punishment as measure.

sentences.zh: 割不忍之恩，行至公之法。

translations.literal: Cutting off kindness one could not bear, he carried out the law of the public.
translations.idiomatic: Cutting off kindness he could not spare, he executed public law.

sentences.zh: 方生貶違，以殺為甚。

translations.literal: At birth he demoted and violated; to kill was the extreme.
translations.idiomatic: At birth she was demoted for violation; execution was the extreme penalty.

sentences.zh: 而神道幽默，禍降未期，雖窮勃履朝，[14]臣不宜糾，既事反人靈，咎將有所，施之取衷，孰為優允？

translations.literal: Yet the spirit's way is subtle; calamity descends before the term; though poor Bo treads the court, [14] your subject should not correct—since the affair reverses human spirits, guilt will have its place; applying it and taking the center, which is the superior allowance?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the spirit's way is subtle and calamity comes unlooked-for; though poor Bo appears in court, [14] I should not judge—since spirits are involved, guilt has its place; which is the better balance?

sentences.zh: 問公羊傳，王者之後郊天曰：神不謬享，帝無妄尊。

translations.literal: Question: The Gongyang Commentary—kings' descendants sacrifice to heaven—says: Spirits do not enjoy mistaken offerings; the emperor has no vain honor.
translations.idiomatic: Question: The Gongyang says kings' descendants sacrifice to heaven—'Spirits do not accept mistaken offerings; the emperor has no empty honor.'

sentences.zh: 介丘偏祀，猶不歆季氏之旅；

translations.literal: Partial sacrifice at Jieqiu still did not accept the Ji clan's journey;
translations.idiomatic: Even partial sacrifice at Jieqiu did not accept the Ji clan's offering;

sentences.zh: 昊天至重，豈可納廢饗之虔？

translations.literal: the vast heaven to the utmost—how can one admit the vain sincerity of a abolished offering?
translations.idiomatic: how can vast heaven accept the vain sincerity of a abolished rite?

sentences.zh: 唐虞已往，事無斯典；

translations.literal: Before Tang and Yu there was no such canon;
translations.idiomatic: Before Tang and Yu there was no such canon;

sentences.zh: 三后已降，始見其文。

translations.literal: after the Three Sovereigns it first appears in writing.
translations.idiomatic: after the Three Sovereigns it first appears in writing.

sentences.zh: 揖讓之冑，禮不上通，昏瘉後燼，四圭是主。

translations.literal: The yielding succession's descendants—ritual does not ascend to communicate; the dim and feeble last embers—the four jade scepters are the lord.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants of yielding succession do not ascend in ritual; the last embers of a fallen house should not hold the four jades.

sentences.zh: 此便至道相承，乾無二統。

translations.literal: This then is the utmost way succeeding one another; Qian has no second unity.
translations.idiomatic: This is the utmost succession of the Way; Heaven admits no second lord.

sentences.zh: 純風既詖，玄牡肆尊，禮不虛革，庶昭異聞。

translations.literal: Pure wind already perverted, the dark ox is wildly honored; ritual is not vainly changed—may it clarify the different report.
translations.idiomatic: When pure custom is corrupted, the dark ox is wildly honored; ritual should not change in vain—may this clarify the issue.

sentences.zh: 問穀梁傳，魯僖三十一年夏四月，「卜郊不從，乃免牲」，傳曰「乃者，亡乎人之辭也」曰：樂以觀風，禮為教本，其細已甚，民不堪命。
