translations.literal: Question: The Guliang Commentary—Lu Xigong year 31 summer fourth month, 'divined the suburban sacrifice and it was not followed, then the victim was released'—the commentary says 'then means the word of a man perishing'—says: Music observes the wind; ritual is the root of teaching—its minutiae already extreme, the people cannot bear the command.
translations.idiomatic: Question: Guliang on Lu Xigong's failed suburban divination—'then' means the words of a perishing man—'Music observes the wind; ritual is the root of teaching—when minutiae grow extreme, the people cannot bear the burden.'

sentences.zh: 齊不加兵，屈於周典。

translations.literal: Qi did not add troops, yielding to Zhou's canon.
translations.idiomatic: Qi did not add troops, yielding to Zhou's canon.

sentences.zh: 僖公魯之盛君，告誡虔祀，穆卜迎吉，而休徵不至。

translations.literal: Duke Xi was Lu's flourishing lord; he admonished with sincere sacrifice, reverently divined to welcome auspiciousness, yet good omens did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xi was Lu's flourishing lord; he sacrificed sincerely and divined reverently, yet good omens did not come.

sentences.zh: 若推咎於天，則神不棄鑒；

translations.literal: If pushing blame to heaven, then spirits do not abandon the mirror;
translations.idiomatic: If blame lies with heaven, spirits do not abandon the mirror;

sentences.zh: 歸愆於人，則頌聲宜替。

translations.literal: returning fault to man, then eulogistic song should cease.
translations.idiomatic: if fault lies with man, praise should cease.

sentences.zh: 既命龜失辰，靈威弗眷，郊享不從，配天斯缺。

translations.literal: Having ordered the tortoise and lost the season, numinous majesty did not look; the suburban offering was not followed—matching heaven was thereby lacking.
translations.idiomatic: The tortoise was ordered at the wrong season; numinous majesty did not attend; the suburban rite failed—heaven was not matched.

sentences.zh: 即傳所言，殆非虛美，何承而制？

translations.literal: As the commentary's words say, it is probably not empty praise—on what basis to establish regulation?
translations.idiomatic: As the commentary says, this is hardly empty praise—on what basis should regulation stand?

sentences.zh: 問尚書胤征，羲和詰其罪，乃季秋月，朔辰弗合於房曰：衡紀不移，日月有度。

translations.literal: Question: In the Venerated Documents, Yin Campaign, Xi and He are charged with crime—yet it was the eighth month, new moon, the morning star not joining in the House—says: The balance mark does not move; sun and moon have measure.
translations.idiomatic: Question: In the Documents' Yin Campaign, Xi and He are charged though it was the eighth month and the morning star did not meet in the House—'The balance mark does not move; sun and moon have measure.'

sentences.zh: 炎涼啟辰，次舍無代。

translations.literal: Heat and cold open the seasons; lodges have no replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Heat and cold open the seasons; lodges have no replacement.

sentences.zh: 履端屢臻，歸餘成閏。

translations.literal: Treading the beginning repeatedly arrives; returning remainder completes the intercalation.
translations.idiomatic: The year begins repeatedly; intercalation completes the remainder.

sentences.zh: 是以爰命羲和，升準徂節，使晷數應時，火流協運。

translations.literal: Therefore Xi and He were ordered to ascend the standard and go to the nodes, making gnomon numbers answer to the seasons and fire's flow harmonize with fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Xi and He were ordered to align the calendar so gnomon and seasons matched.

sentences.zh: 致望舒後律，耀靈爽次。

translations.literal: Making Wang Shu lag in regulation, Yao Ling miss the sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Making the moon lag and the sun miss its sequence.

sentences.zh: 即官闕永，容可為愆。

translations.literal: That the office was lacking for long could be fault.
translations.idiomatic: Long neglect of office could be fault.

sentences.zh: 玄象一差，未成巨戾。

translations.literal: One astral discrepancy—not yet a great crime.
translations.idiomatic: One astral discrepancy is not yet great crime.

sentences.zh: 且杪秋豈回星之辰，授衣非合璧之月。

translations.literal: Moreover the end of autumn—how is it the season of retrograde stars? Granting garments is not appropriate; accumulated fault adds execution;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover late autumn is not the season of retrograde stars; mis-timed garments are fault enough—

sentences.zh: 敍食弗當，積失加誅；

translations.literal: temporary deviation in measure then meets extinction.
translations.idiomatic: must temporary deviation in measure warrant extinction?

sentences.zh: 律度暫差，便遘殄絕。

translations.literal: The benevolent man's army—righteousness does not rise in vain;
translations.idiomatic: The army of the benevolent does not rise without cause;

sentences.zh: 仁者之兵，義不妄興；

translations.literal: the king's wrath suddenly rises—there must be a different explanation.
translations.idiomatic: the king's wrath must have a different explanation.

sentences.zh: 王赫斯舉，將有異說。

translations.literal: Question: In the Mao Odes, 'In the tenth month intercourse, on the new day xinmao the sun was eclipsed—also very ugly'—says: Sun and moon complete the cycle; lodges have constancy; solstice and equinox—no omen of fault.
translations.idiomatic: Question: Mao Odes—'Tenth month, new day xinmao, eclipse—very ugly'—'Sun and moon complete the cycle; solstice points are not faults.'

sentences.zh: 問毛詩，「十月之交，朔日辛卯，日有食之，亦孔之醜」曰：日月次周，行舍有常，分至之候，不為愆咎。

translations.literal: Now the same morning yet becoming deep violation—solely because metal and wood mutually injure, pointing to the day it becomes omen.
translations.idiomatic: Why is the same morning deeply inauspicious? Because metal and wood mutually injure, making the day an omen.

sentences.zh: 今同之辰而為深戾者，專以金木相殘，指日成釁。

translations.literal: Pushing steps not uniform—can it be so?
translations.idiomatic: Astronomical steps differ—can this be so?

sentences.zh: 推步不一，容可如之。

translations.literal: If the reproof appears at proper yang, the day's stem wuwu, birth and restraint mutually follow, like son returning to mother—yet by yin and yang can there be no deep taboo?
translations.idiomatic: If the reproof appears at proper yang on wuwu day, birth and restraint follow like son to mother—can yin and yang have no deep taboo?

sentences.zh: 若謫見正陽，日維戊午，生育相因，猶子歸母，但以陰陽得無深忌乎？

translations.literal: If it is taboo, the new moon should also be calamity;
translations.idiomatic: If it is taboo, the new moon should also be calamity;

sentences.zh: 若為忌也，朔亦應為災；

translations.literal: if not taboo, why should xinmao alone become ugly?
translations.idiomatic: if not taboo, why is xinmao alone ugly?

sentences.zh: 如不忌也，辛卯豈獨成醜？

translations.literal: if not taboo, why should xinmao alone become ugly?
translations.idiomatic: if not taboo, why is xinmao alone ugly?

sentences.zh: 且舉凡之始，以屬月時，繫之在日，有爽明例。

translations.literal: Moreover raising the fan's beginning attaches to the month's season; tying it to the day has a clear contrary example.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the fan's beginning attaches to the month; tying it to the day has clear contrary examples.

sentences.zh: 義不妄構，理用何依？

translations.literal: Righteousness does not fabricate vainly—on what principle does it rely?
translations.idiomatic: Righteousness does not fabricate vainly—on what principle does it rely?

sentences.zh: 問論語，河不出圖，泣麟自傷曰：聖人禀靈天地，資識未形，齊生死於一同，等榮辱於彼我。

translations.literal: Question: In the Analects, the river does not produce the chart, weeping over the unicorn in self-injury—says: The sage receives spirit from heaven and earth; knowledge and insight before form; equalizing life and death in one, equating honor and shame in that and this.
translations.idiomatic: Question: Analects—'The river produced no chart; he wept over the unicorn'—'The sage receives spirit from heaven and earth, equalizing life and death and honor and shame.'

sentences.zh: 孔子自生不辰，從心告齒，樂正既修，素王斯著。

translations.literal: Confucius from birth was untimely; from the heart he told his years; the Director of Music was already cultivated, the uncrowned king was thereby manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius was born untimely; the music master was trained and the uncrowned king thereby appeared.

sentences.zh: 方興吾已之歎，結反袂之悲，進涉無上之心，退深負杖之懼。

translations.literal: Just as he rose came the sigh of 'it is I'; ending with the grief of turning back the sleeve, advancing involved the heart of nothing above, retreating deep was the fear of leaning on the staff.
translations.idiomatic: He sighed 'it is I' and ended in grief of turning the sleeve—advancing with heart of nothing above, retreating in fear of the staff.

sentences.zh: 聖達之理，無乃缺如？

translations.literal: Sage penetration of principle—is it not lacking?
translations.idiomatic: Sage penetration of principle—is it not lacking?

sentences.zh: 符璽郎王神貴答之，名為辯疑，合成十卷，亦有可觀。

translations.literal: Seal and tally officer Wang Shengui answered it, named Discerning Doubts, compiled in ten scrolls—also worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: Seal Officer Wang Shengui answered in Discerning Doubts in ten scrolls—also worth viewing.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝時奏上之。

translations.literal: In the time of the deposed emperor it was memorialized upward.
translations.idiomatic: It was submitted in the reign of the deposed emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝親自執卷，與神貴往復，嘉其用心，特除神貴子鴻彥為奉朝請。

translations.literal: The emperor personally held the scroll and went back and forth with Shengui, commending his intent, and specially made Shengui's son Hongyan a Gentleman at Court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally debated the text with Shengui, praised his effort, and specially made Shengui's son Hongyan a court gentleman.

sentences.zh: 景先子延祐，武定末，太子家令。

translations.literal: Jingxian's son Yanyou at the end of Wuding was Master of the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian's son Yanyou, late in Wuding, was master of the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 景遠，字叔遐。

translations.literal: Jingyuan, courtesy name Shuxia.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan, whose courtesy name was Shuxia.

sentences.zh: 重然諾，好施與。

translations.literal: He greatly valued promises and loved giving.
translations.idiomatic: He valued his word and was generous.

sentences.zh: 頻歲凶儉，分贍宗親，又於通衢以食餓者，存濟甚眾。

translations.literal: In successive years of famine and dearth he divided support among the clan, and at the public road he fed the hungry—preserving and aiding very many.
translations.idiomatic: In years of famine he supported his clan and fed the hungry at the roadside, saving many lives.

sentences.zh: 平原劉郁行經齊兗之境，忽遇劫賊，已殺十餘人。

translations.literal: Liu Yu of Pingyuan was traveling through the Qi and Yan region when he suddenly encountered bandits who had already killed more than ten people.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu of Pingyuan was traveling through Qi and Yan when he met bandits who had already killed more than ten people.

sentences.zh: 次至郁，郁呼曰：「與君鄉近，何忍見殺！」

translations.literal: When it came to Yu he called out: "I am near your township—how can you bear to kill me!"
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Yu he cried, "I am from your region—how can you kill me!"

sentences.zh: 賊曰：「若言鄉里，親親是誰？」

translations.literal: The bandits said: "If you speak of township, who is your kin?"
translations.idiomatic: The bandits asked, "If you claim kinship, who is your relative?"

sentences.zh: 郁曰：「齊州主簿房陽是我姨兄。」

translations.literal: Yu said: "Fang Yang of Qi Province's chief clerk is my mother's sister's son."
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "Fang Yang, chief clerk in Qi Province, is my cousin."

sentences.zh: 陽是景遠小字。

translations.literal: Yang was Jingyuan's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: Yang was Jingyuan's childhood name.

sentences.zh: 賊曰：「我食其粥得活，何得殺其親！」

translations.literal: The bandits said: "We lived on his porridge and survived—how can we kill his kin!"
translations.idiomatic: They said, "We survived on his porridge—how can we kill his kin!"

sentences.zh: 遂還衣服，蒙活者二十餘人。

translations.literal: They then returned his clothes; more than twenty people were spared.
translations.idiomatic: They returned his clothes and spared more than twenty lives.

sentences.zh: 景遠好史傳，不為章句。

translations.literal: Jingyuan loved historical narratives and did not compose parallel prose.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan loved history and did not write parallel prose.

sentences.zh: 天性小急，不類家風，然事二兄至謹，撫養兄孤恩訓甚篤。

translations.literal: By nature he was quick-tempered, unlike the family manner, yet he served his two elder brothers with utmost care and raised his elder brothers' orphans with very earnest instruction.
translations.idiomatic: He was quick-tempered unlike the family norm, yet served his elder brothers devotedly and raised their orphans with great care.

sentences.zh: 益州刺史傅豎眼慕其名義，啟為昭武府功曹參軍，以母老不應，豎眼頗恨之。

translations.literal: Inspector Fu Shuyan of Yizhou admired his reputation and integrity and memorialized him as Merit Officer in the Zhaowu headquarters; because his mother was old he did not accept, and Shuyan was quite resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Fu Shuyan admired him and offered a staff post; he declined because his mother was old, to Shuyan's displeasure.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 子敬道，永熙中，開府參軍事。

translations.literal: His son Jingdao in the Yongxi era was staff officer in the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingdao served on a headquarters staff in the Yongxi era.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：嚴稜夙款可嘉。

translations.literal: The historian says: Yan Leng's long-standing sincerity was commendable.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Yan Leng's early good faith was commendable.

sentences.zh: 脩之晚有誠効。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi in later years had loyal effect.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi proved loyal in his later years.

sentences.zh: 唐和萬里慕義，歸身著績。

translations.literal: Tang He for ten thousand li yearned for righteousness and upon returning showed achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Tang He came from afar in loyalty and achieved merit upon submission.

sentences.zh: 休賓窮而委質。

translations.literal: Xiubin in extremity entrusted his person.
translations.idiomatic: Xiubin, brought to bay, entrusted himself to the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 法壽、伯玉末能投命。

translations.literal: Fashou and Boyu at the end could not throw themselves on the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Fashou and Boyu in the end could not fully submit to the mandate.

sentences.zh: 景伯兄弟，儒風雅業，良可稱焉。

translations.literal: The Jingbo brothers—Confucian wind and elegant achievement—may truly be praised.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingbo brothers' Confucian cultivation and elegant achievement are truly praiseworthy.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Textual collation notes

sentences.zh: 晉昌冥安人也 諸本「冥」作「宜」，北史卷二七唐和傳作「冥」。

translations.literal: Jinchang Ming'an people—all editions read "宜" for "冥"; the History of the Northern Dynasties biography of Tang He reads "冥."
translations.idiomatic: For 'native of Ming'an in Jinchang,' editions read 宜 for 冥; the Northern History Tang He biography has 冥.

sentences.zh: 按冥安，漢舊縣，因冥水得名，北周時始省，見元和志卷四０瓜州晉昌縣條及隋書卷二九地理志上敦煌郡常樂縣注。

translations.literal: Ming'an was an old Han county, named for the Ming River; it was abolished only in the Northern Zhou—see Yuanhe Gazetteer, juan 40, Jinchang County, and Geography of the Sui, juan 29, Dunhuang Commandery, Changle County note.
translations.idiomatic: Ming'an was an old Han county named for the Ming River, abolished under Northern Zhou—see Yuanhe Gazetteer 40 and Sui Geography 29.

sentences.zh: 「宜」字訛，今據北史改。

translations.literal: The character "宜" is erroneous; the text is now changed according to the Northern History.
translations.idiomatic: 宜 is a corruption; the text now follows the Northern History.

sentences.zh: 今在升城 諸本脫「在」字，今據冊府卷四二六

translations.literal: Now in Shengcheng—all editions omit the character "在"; it is now supplemented according to Cefu Yuangui, juan 426 (p. 5076).
translations.idiomatic: All editions omit 在 in 'now in Shengcheng'; it is restored from Cefu Yuangui 426.

sentences.zh: 〈五０七六頁〉
補。

translations.literal: Supplemented.
translations.idiomatic: Supplemented.

sentences.zh: 固執不作 諸本「固」訛「因」，今據北史卷三九劉休賓傳、冊府

translations.literal: Stubbornly would not write—all editions write "因" erroneously for "固"; now changed according to the Northern History, juan 39, Liu Xiubin biography, and Cefu Yuangui (same juan and page).
translations.idiomatic: For 'stubbornly would not write,' editions wrongly have 因 for 固; corrected per Northern History 39 and Cefu Yuangui.

sentences.zh: 〈同上卷頁〉

translations.literal: 〈same juan and page〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈same juan and page〉

sentences.zh: 改。

translations.literal: Changed.
translations.idiomatic: Changed.

sentences.zh: 卿之所訴 諸本「訴」訛「許」，今據冊府卷八三四

translations.literal: What you plead—all editions write "許" erroneously for "訴"; now changed according to Cefu Yuangui, juan 834 (p. 9904).
translations.idiomatic: For 'what you plead,' editions wrongly have 許 for 訴; corrected per Cefu Yuangui 834.

sentences.zh: 〈九九０四頁〉
改。

translations.literal: Changed.
translations.idiomatic: Changed.

sentences.zh: 拜協律中郎 諸本「中郎」作「郎中」，北史卷三九作「中郎」。

translations.literal: Appointed Harmonizer-in-Chief—all editions read "郎中" for "中郎"; the Northern History, juan 39, reads "中郎."
translations.idiomatic: For Harmonizer-in-Chief, editions read 郎中 for 中郎; Northern History 39 has 中郎.

sentences.zh: 按卷一一三官氏志載太和前品令、通典卷二五太常屬官，魏有「協律中郎」，此傳誤倒作「郎中」，今乙正。

translations.literal: According to Offices and Clans, juan 113, the pre-Taihe rank tables, and Tongdian, juan 25, Grand Steward subordinates, Wei had "Harmonizer-in-Chief"; this biography inverts the title as "郎中"—now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Wei rank lists and Tongdian 25 show 協律中郎; the biography's 郎中 is an inversion—now corrected.

sentences.zh: 二子法鳳法武 冊府卷九四０

translations.literal: Two sons Fafeng and Fawu—Cefu Yuangui, juan 940 (p. 11067),
translations.idiomatic: For the two sons Fafeng and Fawu, Cefu Yuangui 940 (p. 11067)

sentences.zh: 〈一一０六七頁〉

translations.literal: reads "虎" for "武."
translations.idiomatic: reads 虎 for 武.

sentences.zh: 按北史卷三九也作「武」。

translations.literal: The Northern History, juan 39, also reads "武."
translations.idiomatic: Northern History 39 also has 武.

sentences.zh: 疑魏書本作「虎」，北史避唐諱改，後人又據北史改此傳。

translations.literal: It is suspected the Wei History originally read "虎" and the Northern History changed it to avoid Tang taboo; later men again changed this biography according to the Northern History.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei History may originally have had 虎, changed in Northern History for Tang taboo, then copied back here.

sentences.zh: 冊府所據尚是未改舊本。

translations.literal: The Cefu Yuangui still reflects the unaltered old text.
translations.idiomatic: Cefu Yuangui preserves the older reading.

sentences.zh: 但別無他證，今仍之。

translations.literal: But there is no other evidence; the text is retained as is.
translations.idiomatic: Without further evidence the text is retained.

sentences.zh: 母子皆出家為尼 北史卷三九「尼」下有「僧」字。

translations.literal: Mother and sons all left home to become nuns—the Northern History, juan 39, after "nuns" has the character "僧."
translations.idiomatic: After 'became nuns' Northern History 39 adds 僧.

sentences.zh: 張森楷云：「母為尼，子不應為尼，有『僧』字是。」

translations.literal: Zhang Senkai says: "If the mother became a nun, the son should not become a nun; the character 'monk' is correct."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Senkai notes: the mother became a nun, the sons monks—僧 is correct.

sentences.zh: 以功賜爵壯武侯加平遠將軍 錢氏考異卷二八云：「按上文，法壽已授平遠將軍矣，不應更加「平遠」之號，前後當有一誤。

translations.literal: For merit enfeoffed Marquis of Zhuangwu and added General Who Pacifies the Distance—Qian Daxin's Collected Variants, juan 28, says: "According to the text above, Fashou had already been appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance; he should not again receive the 'Pacifies the Distance' title—one of the two must be wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Daxin notes Fashou was already General Who Pacifies the Distance; the duplicated title suggests error.

sentences.zh: 考房彥謙碑

translations.literal: Examining the stele of Fang Yanzhi,
translations.idiomatic: Examining Fang Yanzhi's stele,

sentences.zh: 〈金石萃編卷四三〉

translations.literal: 〈Collected Inscriptions on Metal and Stone, juan 43〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Collected Inscriptions on Metal and Stone 43〉

sentences.zh: 述其先世，云法壽以魏郡太守立功歸魏，封莊武侯、

translations.literal: it narrates his forebears, saying Fashou for merit as Administrator of Wei Commandery returned to Wei and was enfeoffed Marquis of Zhuanghou,
translations.idiomatic: his forebears show Fashou enfeoffed Marquis of Zhuanghou after serving as Administrator of Wei,

sentences.zh: 〈『莊』、『壯』二文古相通。〉

translations.literal: 〈the graphs 'Zhuang' and 'Zhuang' are interchangeable in antiquity.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈莊 and 壯 were interchangeable anciently.〉

sentences.zh: 使持節、龍驤將軍、東冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Bearer of the Staff, General of the Dragon Cavalry, Inspector of Eastern Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Bearer of the Staff, General of the Dragon Cavalry, Inspector of Eastern Ji.

sentences.zh: 然則後所加者蓋龍驤將軍也。

translations.literal: Thus what was later added was probably General of the Dragon Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The later addition was probably General of the Dragon Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 平遠將軍第四品，龍驤將軍第三品，故云『加』。」

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the Distance is fourth rank; General of the Dragon Cavalry is third rank—hence the word 'added.'"
translations.idiomatic: Pacifies the Distance is fourth rank, Dragon Cavalry third—hence 'added.'"

sentences.zh: 逼宣明為太守 按元愉敗後，宣明如何，傳不應一無交待，此句下當有脫文。

translations.literal: Forced Xuanming to serve as administrator—after Yuan Yu's defeat, how Xuanming fared should not be left wholly unreported; there must be lost text below this sentence.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Yu forced Xuanming to serve as administrator, the account breaks off—text is missing below.

sentences.zh: 高祖聽之 諸本「祖」作「宗」，獨局本作「祖」。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu permitted it—all editions read "宗" for "祖"; only the Juye edition reads "祖."
translations.idiomatic: Editions read 宗 for 祖 in 'Gaozu permitted'; the Juye edition has 祖.

sentences.zh: 按上文作「高祖」。

translations.literal: The text above reads "Emperor Gaozu."
translations.idiomatic: The passage above reads Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 伯玉城破被擒在元宏

translations.literal: Boyu's city taken and capture occurred under Yuan Hong
translations.idiomatic: Boyu's capture occurred under Emperor Gaozu (Yuan Hong)

sentences.zh: 〈高祖〉

translations.literal: 〈Emperor Gaozu〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Emperor Gaozu〉

sentences.zh: 時，「宗」字顯誤，今從局本。

translations.literal: the character "宗" is clearly erroneous; the Juye edition is followed.
translations.idiomatic: 宗 is clearly wrong; the Juye reading is followed.

sentences.zh: 及弟妓亡 北史卷三九房景伯傳無「妓」字，冊府卷八五二

translations.literal: When the younger brother's concubine died—the Northern History, juan 39, Fang Jingbo biography, lacks the character "concubine"; Cefu Yuangui, juan 852 (p. 10126),
translations.idiomatic: Northern History 39 omits 妓; Cefu Yuangui 852 (p. 10126)

sentences.zh: 〈一０一二六頁〉

translations.literal: reads "妹" for "妓."
translations.idiomatic: reads 妹 for 妓.

sentences.zh: 疑「弟」字下本是其弟之名，訛作「妓」，原作何字，已不可知，北史遂徑刪去。

translations.literal: It is suspected that below "younger brother" there was originally the younger brother's name, corrupted to "concubine"; the original graph cannot be known and the Northern History simply deleted it.
translations.idiomatic: Below 'younger brother' a name may have been corrupted to 妓; Northern History deleted it.

sentences.zh: 冊府當是以意改作「妹」，按照當時社會禮俗，於妹喪不會那樣重視。

translations.literal: Cefu Yuangui probably changed it to "younger sister" by conjecture; according to the ritual customs of the time, mourning for a younger sister would not receive such weight.
translations.idiomatic: Cefu Yuangui likely conjectured 妹; ritual custom would not require such mourning for a sister.

sentences.zh: 廷尉卿崔光韶好標牓人物 諸本「光」作「先」，冊府

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Cui Guangshao loved to label men of character—all editions read "先" for "光"; Cefu Yuangui (same juan and page)
translations.idiomatic: Editions read 先 for 光 in Cui Guangshao's name; Cefu Yuangui has 光.

sentences.zh: 〈同上卷頁〉

translations.literal: 〈same juan and page〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈same juan and page〉

sentences.zh: 作「光」。

translations.literal: reads "光."
translations.idiomatic: reads 光.

sentences.zh: 按崔光韶附卷六六崔亮傳，「先」字訛，今據改。

translations.literal: According to the attached biography in juan 66, Cui Liang biography, "先" is erroneous; now changed accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guangshao's biography in juan 66 shows 先 is wrong; corrected accordingly.

sentences.zh: 況斬焉初之創巨方始 語意晦澀。

translations.literal: How much more in the case of the hem—at the first founding the great wound just begins—the meaning is obscure.
translations.idiomatic: The phrase about the hem and 'great wound just begins' is obscure.

sentences.zh: 疑「初之」為「之初」誤倒，讀作「況斬焉之初，創巨方始」，但無他據，今姑於「斬焉」斷句，「初之」屬下讀。

translations.literal: It is suspected "初之" is an inversion of "之初"; read as "how much more at the first of the hem, the great wound just begins"—but without other evidence, for now a break is made after "hem" and "初之" is read with what follows.
translations.idiomatic: 初之 may be inverted 之初; without evidence the line is punctuated after 斬焉.

sentences.zh: 雖窮勃履朝 按齊人殺哀姜，見左傳閔二年。

translations.literal: Though poor Bo treads the court—see Zuozhuan, Min year 2, for the Qi killing of Ai Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: See Zuozhuan Min 2 for the Qi killing of Ai Jiang.

sentences.zh: 「窮勃」不知所出。

translations.literal: "Poor Bo" has no known source.
translations.idiomatic: The phrase 'poor Bo' (窮勃) has no known source.
